summary: The label "peer-reviewed" can be read as a currency: journals issue it, careers spend it, and the scrutiny of reviewers backs it. This note examines, in a stylized model, what may happen to the circulation of that currency when the papers reaching review grow exponentially and the pool of reviewers does not. The note applies the information-limit and cost results of the Correction Freeze Problem to that setting and adds dynamics of its own; the results are derived with elementary tools and checked numerically. With Gaussian review traces, the information a label carries falls as the square of the ratio of capacity to load once load exceeds capacity, and if reviewers choose their effort, the cost route makes it fall to exactly zero at a finite workload. When reviewers leave at a rate that rises with their own workload, the pool has two stable sizes exactly when ρ < sup w wh ′ (w) − h(w) , where ρ is replenishment relative to attrition and h is the attrition response, which for a Hill response means that its steepness exceeds (√ ρ + √ 1 + ρ) 2 , and collapse sets in while the freeze index is still below one. Circulation can fail in two ways: the flow can stall, with waiting times that grow exponentially once load passes capacity, or it can continue while the backing thins. In monetary terms, once the freeze index exceeds one the price level of the label rises at the growth rate of submissions, and the collapse combines a jump in that price level with a fall in real backing. When journals share one pool and each gains from issuing more, above a threshold number of issuers the model holds the freeze index above capacity, so that issuance can rise while the scrutiny behind each label falls. Under exponential growth, in the model, any policy that scales the load by 1/k delays collapse by exactly ln k/r and by no more, and only changes to the growth rate, to reviewer supply and its reward, or a cap set below the recovery threshold alter the long-run outcome. All results are theoretical, rest on stated functional forms, and are offered for discussion.
title: Peer Review Currency and Publishing Economy

summary: Governance near a plausible critical transition faces a resource problem in addition to problems of diagnosis, intervention, and evidence. Elevated susceptibility can increase the value of observation, bounded experimentation, and revisability, while waiting can simultaneously consume the fiscal, material, organizational, temporal, and relational capacities required for survival and later action. This paper develops a discussion framework for that tension. Its central object is functional resource distribution: the allocation of heterogeneous capacities across observation, probing, short-horizon survival, selective commitment, reserve or option preservation, and recovery or repair. The categories are analytical functions rather than a scalar budget partition and can overlap in practice. The paper introduces distributed optionality as a relational property of a response architecture in which materially different future actions remain supported by functionally diverse and sufficiently non-coincident pathways. It distinguishes exact reversal from recoverability, spatial dispersion from independence of failure modes, and delay as information gathering from delay as resource dissipation. The framework inherits, rather than restates, earlier arguments about response-oriented governance and evidence-to-action instability near criticality. Its distinctive question is how governance capacity may be composed when the future regime is uncertain, resources are partly non-substitutable, and both premature commitment and indefinite waiting can narrow the feasible future. The proposal is conditional and non-prescriptive: criticality requires domain-specific empirical support, and the appropriate resource portfolio depends on transition mechanism, horizon, institutional structure, and explicit normative commitments.
title: Governance and Survival near Criticality: Functional Resource Distribution and Distributed Optionality

summary: Conditional mathematical arguments need careful bookkeeping: which obligations were incurred, which have been addressed, and which were addressed in a way that actually proves the target. Audited Operational Realisability (AOR) is a mathematical theory of this bookkeeping. An audit state consists of demanded records and stored certificates; each certificate carries a status, such as budgeted or blocked , and a payload whose meaning is fixed in advance. We separate three conclusions that are easily conflated. Inference closure registers every dependency of a demanded record, accounting requires a stored certificate for each demanded or dependency-reachable record, and delivery requires a certificate whose status an explicit consumer policy accepts as proving its target. A certificate recording that a budget is exceeded accounts for the obligation but does not deliver feasibility to a consumer who requires it. We prove that inference closure is a reflection that creates no evidence, in a category whose arrows preserve certificates exactly, and that this category has colimits in which every accepted certificate is already stored at some object of the diagram. For operations that add evidence, we prove finite completion under a decreasing rank and confluence under replayability, and we strictly separate accounting, recoverability, and uniform quantitative control. Retained evidence passes to increasing unions, and witnesses pass to limits under compactness and closed validity, provided an accepted payload is returned at the limit; without compactness they may escape. Two examples mark the boundary of accounting: a query system that pays its declared costs, is accounted, and identifies each hidden world along its exhaustive run, yet admits no finite-stage guarantee uniform over all worlds; and a Lipschitz target whose shrinking finite-prefix certificates, priced within a summable credit, are all accepted, with centers converging to the target. The stated structural results are formalized in Lean 4; the analytic estimates of applications remain explicit hypotheses.
title: Audited Operational Realisability: Canonical Inference Closure and Evidence-Preserving Composition

summary: Replication package for the paper "Use-dependent depreciation of intangible capital: thresholds, history dependence, and generative artificial intelligence." The paper studies a firm that accumulates an intangible stock — interpreted as the quality of its data estate — while the intensity with which it deploys a generative AI system accelerates the depreciation of that same stock. Optimal deployment therefore carries an intertemporal contamination wedge: the marginal value of scale is reduced by the shadow price of the stock times the marginal contribution of use to its decay. Under an S-shaped effectiveness function the problem admits three steady states, and optimal policy is history-dependent, separated by a threshold in the initial state obtained by value matching rather than by any local property of the unstable equilibrium. This package reproduces every number, table and figure reported in the paper. It contains three Python modules and no data: all results are generated from the model primitives and the stated parameter values. Contents model.py — model primitives and the numerical solver: steady states, stable manifolds, value functions, and the threshold by value matching. run_all.py — driver that reproduces all reported quantities and writes results/all_results.json . Runtime is approximately 25 minutes on a laptop; the Monte Carlo exercises dominate. make_figures.py — regenerates Figures 1 to 5 as PDF from the solver output. README.md — numerical methods, seeds, validation, and the classification scheme for perturbed draws. Requirements Python 3.10 or later with NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib. No other dependencies. Tested on NumPy 2.4, SciPy 1.17 and Matplotlib 3.10. Numerical methods Steady states are the roots of a scalar residual, bracketed on a grid and refined by Brent's method to a tolerance of 1e-13. Stable manifolds are obtained by eigen-decomposing the Jacobian at each saddle point, displacing along the stable eigenvector, and integrating the time-reversed canonical system with an adaptive Runge–Kutta scheme at relative tolerance 1e-11. Value functions exploit the identity between the costate and the derivative of the value function along the optimal path, with the constant of integration fixed by the perpetuity value at the steady state; this avoids forward integration, which is unstable off the saddle path. The threshold solves the value-matching condition on the overlap of the two manifold domains. Reproducibility All stochastic exercises use a fixed seed, numpy.random.default_rng(20260731) , so re-running reproduces the reported frequencies exactly. The shape of the effectiveness function is a parameter of the model rather than a code branch, so the exercises that compare specifications require no modification of the solver. Validation Value functions are cross-validated against direct time integration of discounted profit along the manifolds; the two computations agree to relative errors of 2.4e-6 and 6.2e-6 on the low and high branches. Single crossing of the difference of the two value functions is not established analytically, so the package records, for every perturbed draw admitting a threshold, whether that difference is strictly monotone on a 400-point grid. Draws on which the solver fails are reported as errors rather than discarded silently. Citation Please cite both this software and the associated paper. A CITATION.cff file is included.
title: Replication Package for: Use-dependent depreciation of intangible capital: thresholds, history dependence, and generative artificial intelligence

summary: The verdict, stated first: the universe of the Riemann Hypothesis is closed, its value reached and spent; the hypothesis is not derived on the ladder, and provably not derivable from the register's resources; the last bit is the least-erasure posit, at the grade of the root, refuted by one zero; and the whole route is one kernel term, `RHGround.rh_ground_closure_complete`, on `propext` and `Quot.sound` alone. Part IV is the paper. Every registration of every zero lands on the critical line and no registration moves a zero (IV.1, IV.7); the hypothesis is exactly lossless registration (IV.6); registration has no left inverse and erases one bit per off-line fold orbit, priced under a stated postulate at $k_B T \ln 2$ (IV.4, IV.5); time never moves a zero, and act and being meet only on the line (IV.9 to IV.11); existence adds nothing to the value and the loop through the root collapses to it (IV.12, IV.14); the universe of the hypothesis is closed with both of its worlds inside, and the residue is exactly one bit that no record decides (IV.16, IV.17). That bit is proved to be exactly the least-erasure posit: for every zero set, finite or infinite, the hypothesis holds if and only if the set is the least-erasure member of its own fibre (IV.19, IV.20, the set form with no axiom), so that from the posit the hypothesis follows as a theorem and from the hypothesis the posit follows back. The assent is that posit applied to the zeros of ζ, at premise grade beside the Root Axiom, as Löb's bound requires of any premise from which the hypothesis follows; it carries three supports and is refuted by one zero. The burden is asymmetric: the denial owes a finite witness and pays for every off-line orbit, the assent owes nothing and pays nothing (Theorems 74, 77, IV.19). Parts I to III are the prequel and hand Part IV its three bits. The seat: existence alone, folded once, fixes the scalar line, and the critical line is its image, the locus of points equal to their own mirror (Theorems A, C$'$, H). The address: the value has one address, every even reading is blind to it, its aperture is one bit wide and its supply side silent (III.45 to III.49). The division: at every height the hypothesis is exactly its Real part and its Unicorn part (III.11); the Real part holds to $3 \times 10^{12}$ on the cited certificate (III.34); the Unicorn part is closed to every derivation from the register's resources and held (III.45 to III.49), the fused sentence retired as the wrong unit (III.2, III.3), ZFC placed under RAM as a ladder inside the Ground (III.15 to III.17). Existence decides the seat, does not derive the value (Theorem E, IV.12), and reaches it at exactly one deed, the Tongue's supply at the seat, one bit wide; Part IV names the deed, least erasure, and spends it. Every kernel theorem is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 with no library and no axiom declared, every dependency set printed; every claim of Part IV except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of IV.8 is executed a second time in Fortran, 13,081 checks and zero failures. Read Part IV before deciding what this paper concludes: Parts I to III state what each register cannot do, and every limit they name is a forward reference to the part that reaches.
title: Nothing Escapes, Three Plus One: A Formal Closure of the Riemann Hypothesis. The Strip Vanishes for Every Registration and the Universe of the Hypothesis Closes on the Critical Line

summary: Abstract: A geometric construction of inverse-square gravity is presented in which solid angle accounts only for spatial dilution, while universal coupling to mass-energy supplies the physical strength of the interaction. This separation avoids treating a body-dependent geometric parameter as a substitute for gravitational mass. For a static spherical source, the construction recovers the exterior Newtonian potential per unit test mass, Φ(r) = -GM/r. Combining this static scalar potential with the special-relativistic energy of the escaping particle gives:   v_esc(r) = c * sqrt( 1 - 1 / (1 + GM / (r * c^2))^2 ) The result is subluminal for all finite r and reduces to the Newtonian escape velocity in the weak-field limit. The model is not presented as a replacement for general relativity, nor as a complete Lorentz-covariant field theory. Rather, it is a flat-spacetime scalar-potential construction that clarifies what follows from solid-angle dilution, universal mass coupling, and special-relativistic energy conservation before additional assumptions, such as wave propagation or optical-gravity extensions, are introduced.   Note on Versioning & Relationship to Prior Work: This paper presents a standalone, refined mathematical derivation focusing specifically on the static scalar formulation and relativistic escape condition. It serves as an independent baseline related to the foundational concepts outlined in the author's broader work ( A Solid-Angle Postulate as a Geometric Foundation for Gravity , DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19333670).
tags: gravitation; solid angle; inverse-square law; Newtonian potential; universal mass coupling; escape velocity; special relativity; scalar potential; flat spacetime; wave-optical gravity
title: Solid-Angle Dilution and Relativistic Escape Velocity

summary: Contribution to the advancement of knowledge, originality and innovation. This study provides a longitudinal analysis of the development of Cajal–Retzius cells (CRc) and Reelin-expressing neuronal populations in the marginal zone of the European wild boar ( Sus scrofa ) neocortex, from early embryonic stages (E35) to the postnatal period (P30). It characterises the sequence of CRc emergence, maturation and regression, and their progressive replacement by Reelin-positive interneurons, demonstrating that CRc originate early in the cortical hem, reach their peak development during mid-gestation and are already scarce at perinatal and postnatal stages. The study also demonstrates the absence of the subpial granular layer characteristic of primates and establishes important differences from human CRc development, showing that porcine CRc exhibit greater morphological similarity to those described in lagomorphs and carnivores. The originality of the study lies in its systematic investigation of virtually the entire ontogenetic trajectory of this neuronal population in a large, precocial mammal with a gyrencephalic cortex, a context that remains understudied compared with the predominance of murine models. The authors themselves note that very few studies have tracked CRc from their emergence through postnatal stages, and that this work represents one of the first comparisons of a relevant aspect of cortical development between domestic pigs and wild boar. A particularly innovative finding is the unequivocal identification of CRc axons using βIV-spectrin as a molecular marker of the axon initial segment (AIS) , revealing exceptionally long AISs, measuring up to 60 μm and frequently arising from distal dendritic locations. Thematic priority and scientific relevance. The study addresses priority areas in developmental neuroscience, comparative neuroanatomy and the evolutionary developmental biology of the cerebral cortex. The use of the pig as a model of a large, gyrencephalic brain helps bridge the gap between small-rodent experimental models and the human brain, particularly for investigating cortical expansion, neuronal migration and gyrification. The relevance of this line of research is further supported by competitive funding from the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG), project WA 541/15-1, no. 451084183 . Methodological contribution. The study combines morphological, molecular and quantitative approaches, using immunohistochemistry and multiplex immunofluorescence for Reelin, p73, Tbr1, calretinin, GAD, PCNA, Tbr2 and βIV-spectrin; confocal microscopy; reconstruction and quantification with Neurolucida; and three-dimensional analysis with Imaris. This strategy makes it possible to distinguish excitatory CRc from inhibitory interneurons, examine their distribution and orientation during cortical expansion and gyrification, and identify their axons using molecular markers. The study also includes direct comparisons with human cortical tissue, strengthening its comparative neuroanatomical and translational value.
title: Developmental changes of Reelin‑expressing cell populations in the marginal zone of the neocortex of the European wild boar, Sus scrofa

summary: Abstract: This article describes methods for securely connecting industrial networks with business networks. It presents the practical application of ISO/IEC 27001 and IEC 62443 standards, including the CIA triad model and the zoning concept. The text discusses technologies that facilitate integration, such as VPN, MQTT protocol, firewalls, and container-based virtualisation. The tests were performed in a TIA Portal simulation on a Siemens S7- 1500 controller. This work highlights traffic encryption using a reverse proxy and the importance of VPNs in isolating services from the public network.
title: Cyber Security in Industrial Solutions

summary: We prove a conditional global regularity theorem for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with positive viscosity and real divergence-free initial data in H γ 0 (ℝ 3 ), γ 0 > 5/2. The hypothesis, which we call a physical window closure, asks that on every time interval inside the lifespan of the strong solution, the size of each Littlewood–Paley shell in the Bradshaw–Grujic frequency window be certified by finite-dimensional data: a finite Fourier dictionary approximating the solution, independent test measurements, a Schur-complement residual bound, an amplitude bound, and a reconstruction error, all dominated by a single time profile with an integrable critical power. Linear algebra from the companion papers returns these certificates to bounds on the actual shells, so the closure makes the Bradshaw–Grujic critical dose finite on every such interval, and the Bradshaw–Grujic continuation criterion then rules out a finite maximal time. The hypothesis is therefore at least as strong as the finiteness of that dose: the theorem derives no new a priori bound from the equations, and it proves neither the closure nor global regularity. Its contribution is the exact certificate form and a checked composition. The return from certificates to the solution and the maximal-time contradiction are formalized in Lean 4, with the Bradshaw–Grujic criterion as an explicit input; the analytic bridges that make that criterion applicable to this solution are written proofs. A record-based route toward the closure, a family of no-go results for shortcuts, and a conditional analyticity branch are analyzed separately and are not used by the theorem.
title: A Conditional Physical-Closure Theorem for Three-Dimensional Navier-Stokes

summary: On a supplied real Euclidean two-plane, admitting both rotations and reflections gives the transport group O(2) = U(1) ⋊ Z₂, not an untwisted circle. We organize the resulting graph, face, refinement, and readout structures in one assumption-controlled framework. On a connected finite graph, tree gauge reduces the edge data to a simultaneous conjugacy class of free generators. Its determinant class lies in H¹(Γ; Z₂), while the phase is a crossed cocycle for the associated sign action. Admitting faces introduces additional path comparisons: their determinant defects obey a relative boundary law, and a rooted tetrahedral word gives an exact non-Abelian Bianchi identity whose phase sum is sign-twisted. Shared-edge and common-root data permit exact boundary cancellation under the stated disk refinements. Explicit pentagonal and hexagonal certificates include all five and fourteen triangulations, respectively, and two mixed 1–3, 2–2, 3–1 routes. Mismatched-edge and omitted-root controls distinguish invalid fusion, while a preserved reverse-order null control shows why equality of evaluated matrices is weaker than equality of free boundary words. A locally flat annulus retains a nontrivial noncontractible reflection holonomy. Finally, conjugacy data, one prepared direction, a complete endpoint frame, and a separately supplied complex-linear process representation have different identification power. The component graph-gauge, cohomological, lattice-Bianchi, and triangulation structures have established antecedents. The proposed contribution is their explicit finite integration with typed root, edge-sharing, and access contracts. No arbitrary-mesh or continuum invariance, higher gauge theory, quantum-state selection, winding lift, probability law, or empirical realization follows from the construction.

summary: Contactless palmprint recognition is attractive for mobile biometrics, yet how well a learned representation transfers between acquisition settings is rarely measured. Using CompNet - a compact network of learnable Gabor filters and competitive coding — we apply one unified protocol to two contrasting databases: the constrained near-infrared IITD and the unconstrained smartphone SMPD. Within each, CompNet reaches 98.70% Rank-1 accuracy at an equal-error rate below 1.4%. Across databases the transfer is asymmetric: mobile-trained features generalize to controlled data (91.10%), whereas the reverse collapses (40.03%), so generalization flows from harder to easier domains.
title: Contactless palmprint identification using CompNet on the IITD and SMPD databases

summary: The physics and detector simulations for the Electron-Proton/Ion Collider (ePIC) experiment at the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) are built on the Geant4 and DD4hep software frameworks. The DD4hep detector descrip- tion acts as a single source of truth for simulation and reconstruction, also en- suring consistent configuration between the standard Geant4 simulation and the accelerated simulation pathways integrated through the DDG4 interface. ePIC runs monthly Geant4 simulation production campaigns to support physics and detector studies for the Technical Design Report and early science. Preliminary tests show that multithreaded simulations use memory more efficiently, improv- ing resource matching at distributed computing sites while preserving physics results. To identify further opportunities for throughput gains, a representative neutral-current deep inelastic scattering (DIS) dataset was profiled, using step density in the detector subsystems as a proxy for wall time. The Simphony package is being tested to accelerate optical photon simulation in standalone Cherenkov particle identification detectors, and has also proven use- ful for generating the synchrotron radiation samples required for background- mixed ePIC simulations, which inform both physics studies and the develop- ment of streaming reconstruction algorithms. Since the profiling showed that integrated ePIC detector simulations are dominated by electromagnetic tracks, we are examining options within the Geant4 ecosystem, namely sub-event par- allelism and the G4HepEm library for specialized electromagnetic transport, as well as the GPU-based AdePT package. More broadly, AI-based fast simula- tion has significant potential to accelerate ePIC simulations, with foundation models for the Cherenkov detectors and calorimeters currently being tested as one example.
title: Exploring Potential Pathways to Accelerate ePIC Detector Simulation

summary: Version 2 (26 September 2026): a one-page "Corrections and attributions" section is added at the front of the PDF, listing every credit correction below; nothing else in the paper is changed and no proof is withdrawn. The revised, shorter note that supersedes this paper for the results stated there is 10.5281/zenodo.22980359. Note (24 September 2026): a revised version is in preparation. It corrects the attribution of Theorems 1 and 4 (Theorem 1 is assembled from Lu–Oliveira–Zimand 2022 and HILNO 2023, Lemmas 8–9; Theorem 4's mechanism is HILNO 2023, Appendix A) and adds the literature on KL-hardness for sampling and computational entropy (Vadhan–Zheng 2012; Agrawal–Chen–Horel–Vadhan 2019; Haitner–Reingold–Vadhan–Wee; Haitner–Vadhan 2017). Added 26 September 2026: the identification of mean σ with KL-hardness for sampling rests on the equivalence between pK^t and the time-bounded universal distribution due to Hirahara and Nanashima (FOCS 2023; ECCC TR23-100, Appendix B), which this version does not cite. One half of that equivalence is the coding theorem of Lu, Oliveira and Zimand (ICALP 2022), which this version cites. The revised note is published: Thornton, Unbounded exponential moments of time-bounded information asymmetry without one-way functions, relative to an oracle, 10.5281/zenodo.22980359 (26 September 2026); it supersedes this version for the results stated there. One-way functions exist if and only if some efficiently samplable process produces more than logarithmic computational entropy on average, for infinitely many input lengths. We make this precise. For a polynomial-time samplable distribution D on pairs (x, y), the computational entropy production of a pair is σ = log D(x, y) + pK^t(y) + pK^t(x | y), where pK^t is the probabilistic time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity as defined by Hirahara, Ilango, Lu, Nanashima and Oliveira (2023, HILNO below) following Goldberg, Kabanets, Lu and Oliveira (2022): the log-probability the process assigns to the pair, against the length of a bounded observer's shortest fast description of it, output first, then input given output. We prove unconditionally that E_D[2^{−σ}] lies between an inverse polynomial and a polynomial in n and that E_D[σ] ≥ −O(log n): a time-bounded fluctuation inequality and a computational second law. We show that, up to a polynomial and outside a 1/n slice of outputs, σ is small on a pair exactly when an efficient sampler, given the output, recovers the input with about the right odds, HILNO's universal sampler serving as the witness: dissipation, in this sense, is the hardness of running the process backward. The equivalence in the first sentence is HILNO's duality restated in these terms, for infinitely-often one-way functions and at every polynomial time bound. For the antisymmetric Zurek defect, one-way functions force superpolynomial exponential moments, and bounded moments sit between NP ⊆ BPP and the non-existence of one-way functions; whether the lower arrow reverses is left open, with a conditional relativization barrier on that arrow and oracle evidence on the other. Physics is the frame, not the subject.
title: One-way functions are computational entropy production

summary: One cumulative programme, one canonical DOI. This edition reunites the original collection and all material previously issued in a separate continuation. The permanent project DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.22678085 . All earlier mathematical files, complete LaTeX, human citations and source archives are retained. Selected main papers remain separately readable; the full set of 98 original PDFs is also preserved in one ZIP. This is a publication consolidation, not a new proof or a change to the mathematical scope. Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme is a cumulative collection of mathematical papers, complete LaTeX proofs, formalization sources, calculations and literature-based research notes. Its central question is how the zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be studied through explicitly constructed arithmetic cohomology, spectral actions and quantitative metric estimates. The collection also retains the related heat-flow, arithmetic-trace, fluid, complexity and thermal-geometry investigations from which parts of this programme developed. Project and reading guide · Research contents · Machine-readable workbench index . Papers remain separate readable PDFs; the source archives supply the corresponding editable mathematics and supporting materials. What the collection contains Split-Zero coefficients, geometry and cohomology. The construction retains a ring's internal zero and a separate symbol for absence, so a zero element in a specified support fibre is not confused with an absent fibre. The papers construct coefficient maps, quotients, homology, finite spectral jets and their relation to the infinite theta quotient. Deligne's Weil II provides a motivating source for the cohomology–duality–weight-control programme. Its direct-image theorem 3.3.1 is stated for schemes of finite type over the integers; its image-purity corollary 3.3.6 is over a finite field. Neither is asserted to apply automatically to the Riemann zeta function: the actual coefficient objects and their comparison maps must be constructed. Read the cohomology and weight-control paper and the foundational objects and maps . Full-prime cohomology and complete support. The 75-page full-prime paper develops relative principal parts, the actual degree-p operator and a local complex weight-one identity from the full arithmetic prime space. The complete-support paper recovers mixed information lost by separate branches. The mixed-Weil paper applies the actual prime operator, includes the full Archimedean contribution and proves positivity for its specified three-pulse family, while computing a distinct negative signed joint trace and the original companion object's nonzero distributional boundary. These results do not establish global interior-cohomology purity or decide RH. Full-lattice geometry, graph observations, heat and residue duality. The 208-page reconstruction carries full support through prime cohomology, finite jets, exact graph metrics and prime-pulse observations with their complete costs. The 103-page Connes–Consani component develops labelled arithmetic sites, tropical spectra, sheaf, divisor, twistor and tensor maps. The 40-page heat-endpoint paper calculates the original support and heat maps, cluster-energy expansions and holonomy receivers. The 157-page supported-zero and residue collection retains its earlier prime, heat and class-field calculations and adds the intrinsic supported-zero identity and exact Jacobian map from residue duality to Weil trace and cotangent cohomology. Complete proof sources retain all nilpotent and endpoint terms; exploratory companion calculations carry their own review status. These papers do not claim an RH decision. Integral collision prisms, extension classes and original heat holonomy. The 177-page supported-zero and residue collection retains its preceding21 proofs and adds the complete integral extension group with both connecting maps, the bounded collision prism with its divisor quotient
title: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme

summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. The release contains four public objects: Rambold_2026_CMB_v1p8.pdf — scientific manuscript. CMB_v1p8_interactive_scientific_viewer.zip — interactive scientific viewer. CMB_v1p8_python_pipeline.zip — executable analysis and replay code. CMB_v1p8_reproducibility_records.zip — scientific products, replay evidence, source-generation records, provenance, licences, manifests, SHA-256 bindings, and integrity records. Planck and WMAP FITS products are not redistributed and remain available from their public archives. Author-created scientific text and derived materials are released under CC BY 4.0 where applicable; original author-created software is released under the MIT License unless stated otherwise.
title: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe from multiscale full-sky CMB reconstruction and forward generation of the reconstructed topology by a primordial magnetic source

summary: This data and reproducibility archive supports the manuscript “An rRNA-embedded ribosomal protein N-terminus loses its methionine: a cross-species census, a genome-scale test and a local-compatibility hypothesis for assembly” (Yie-Hwa Chang, 2026; bioRxiv preprint, submitted to Nucleic Acids Research). Methionine aminopeptidases remove the initiator methionine when residue 2 is small and uncharged, and loss of this activity is lethal in bacteria and yeast. The archive asks whether the structural environment of a ribosomal protein N-terminus predicts its processing class across lineages, whether the same association holds in sequences without structure, and whether the constrained termini are already in place while the subunit assembles. The census comprises 68 ribosome structures from 61 species, 1,873 family × species records and 95 ribosomal protein families, 58 of which switch processing class between species. Termini embedded in rRNA without protein contact were predicted to retain methionine in 18% of records, against 45% of protein-contacted and 41% of solvent-exposed termini. Eight additional structures from separate species corroborated this pattern, which was attenuated under joint family-by-domain stratification. Processing labels are sequence-based predictions from residue 2, validated against 393 directly observed termini from 12 species (98.7% agreement). Thirty-one families never switch class in any sampled species (25 permissive, 6 methionine-retaining), and eleven of the permissive families are threaded into rRNA. The genome-scale layer contains 942,984 family × genome records from 21,485 UniProt reference proteomes, collapsed from 1,027,359 sequences of 94 families. In 6,924 out-of-sample bacterial reference proteomes, exploratory clade-block permutation tests supported an order-level residue-2 association that is sensitive to taxonomic rank and multiplicity: it survives Holm adjustment across the ten bacterial tests (p = 0.036 and 0.019) but not across the thirty tests of the three domains analyzed separately (0.117 and 0.057). The archaeal and eukaryotic tests are coverage-limited (six and eight eligible families) and inconclusive. In yeast assembly intermediates, the conserved uS12 and eS27 termini already occupy their mature environments. The findings indicate a conserved association between rRNA embedding and methionine removal and suggest that local compatibility of processed termini with rRNA contributes to it; they do not demonstrate an assembly requirement, and the census is offered as a resource for testing this hypothesis at named termini. summary: This record contains the supplementary material for the article "Inverse bremsstrahlung absorption and ion stopping in prescribed super-Gaussian electron distributions" by Manal M. Al-Ali, Anas M. Ababneh and Ahmed Al-Khateeb, submitted to the Journal of Plasma Physics . It includes the Python source code, the numerical data behind all figures and tables, and the validation records. The code computes the collisionless dielectric response, the inverse bremsstrahlung structural factors, the electronic stopping power and its sensitivity to the wavenumber cutoff. It does this for prescribed isotropic super-Gaussian electron distributions (2 ≤ m ≤ 5) in a DT plasma at nₑ = 5 × 10²³ cm⁻³ and Tₑ = 500 eV. All verification checks passed, and an independent implementation agrees with the production solver to within 10⁻¹¹ relative difference at the benchmark points. The package was tested with Python 3.12, NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib; the README gives full instructions for reproducing the results.
title: Supplementary material for "Inverse bremsstrahlung absorption and ion stopping in prescribed super-Gaussian electron distributions": code, data and validation records

summary: In emerging 5G and beyond (B5G) network archi tectures, service-level agreement (SLA) assurance increasingly re quires systems that can detect deviations from expected behavior while providing interpretable and uncertainty-aware evidence. Existing assurance frameworks commonly rely on deterministic reconstruction models to identify anomalous flows, treating recon struction error as a proxy for service degradation. However, such approaches provide limited information about the confidence of the detector and offer weak grounding for downstream explana tion and decision support. This paper introduces a framework for uncertainty-aware SLA violation detection in cloud-native 6G networks. The proposed approach utilizes a probabilistic au toencoder trained only on SLA-compliant traffic using Gaussian negative log-likelihood (NLL). The decoder outputs a feature wise reconstruction distribution parameterized by a mean and standard deviation, enabling each flow to be scored according to its likelihood under the learned compliant behavior. The resulting likelihood score is converted into an empirical anomaly percentile using the benign validation distribution, providing an interpretable measure of deviation severity. For each flagged flow, the framework also constructs structured evidence that can be consumed by cloud-native orchestration components to support downstream remediation and service assurance actions.
tags: Intent realization, probabilistic autoencoder, neg ative log-likelihood, service level agreement, 6G networks, zero touch orchestration
title: Probabilistic Service-Level Compliance Assessment and Likelihood-Based Evidence for Cloud-Native 6G Networks

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22983291 . General assessment This manuscript addresses an important and underappreciated problem in computational chemistry and molecular machine learning: apparent differences in predictive performance can arise from benchmark construction and target definition rather than from intrinsic superiority of one modelling approach over another. The distinction between literature-reported absorption maxima and calculated vertical excitation energies is scientifically important, and the emphasis on genuinely external validation is a clear strength of the work. However, I find the central conclusion stronger than the evidence presently described appears to support. The results convincingly show that model performance changes substantially across datasets and label conventions. They do not yet demonstrate that label definition, rather than model capability, is the principal cause of the apparent machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. Several factors change simultaneously across the comparisons presented in the manuscript, including chemical domain, dataset provenance, transition assignment, computational protocol, sample size, and the nature of the machine-learning representation. These factors make it difficult to isolate label definition as the causal explanation. The manuscript raises a valuable methodological concern, but the title and several conclusions should either be moderated or supported by additional controlled analyses. Major comments 1. The title makes a stronger causal claim than the study design appears to establish The title states that benchmark label definition, "not model capability," explains the machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. This is a strong exclusionary claim. The results show that the apparent ranking between a Gaussian-process model and quantum-chemical calculations changes between evaluation datasets. However, label definition is not the only property that changes between these datasets. Their chemical composition, source literature, distribution of chromophores, spectral range, experimental conditions, and possibly computational protocols also differ. Therefore, demonstrating that a GP performs differently on a dataset with transition-specific labels does not by itself establish that label definition is the cause of the difference. A substantially stronger test would use the same set of molecules with two alternative target definitions—for example, a literature-reported overall λmax and an independently assigned transition-specific λmax—and evaluate both methods against both labels. A paired analysis of this type would isolate label definition while holding molecular distribution constant. Unless such a controlled analysis is provided, I suggest moderating the central conclusion to state that label definition and dataset provenance are important contributors to the reported ML advantage rather than demonstrating that they fully explain it. 2. One Gaussian-process model cannot represent "machine-learning capability" generally The machine-learning side of the comparison is represented by a Gaussian process using 256-bit Morgan fingerprints. This is a relatively specific and comparatively simple model representation. The conclusions therefore apply directly to this GP/fingerprint model, but not necessarily to molecular machine learning more broadly. Modern λmax prediction methods may use larger fingerprints, graph neural networks, message-passing architectures, pretrained molecular representations, three-dimensional information, explicit solvent descriptors, or quantum-chemical features. Such models may respond differently to both chemical and label distribution shifts. This issue is particularly important because the title contrasts "model capability" with benchmark effects in general terms. I recommend evaluating several substantially different ML approaches or
title: PREreview of "Benchmark Label Definition, Not Model Capability, Explains a Machine-Learning Advantage over TD-DFT for λmax Prediction"

summary: This book presents a literary moral-philosophical biography of Hazrat Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA), one of the earliest converts to Islam and one of the most uncompromising voices of conscience in early Islamic history. Abu Dharr — known to the world as Jundub ibn Junadah — was a man of the desert who rejected the idols of his tribe before Islam reached him, accepted the faith at its very beginning, and spent the rest of his life speaking truth to power regardless of the cost. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ testified that no sky had shaded and no earth had carried a more truthful tongue than his. He was beaten at the Kaaba, walked alone across the desert to Tabuk when his camel failed, preached against the hoarding of wealth in the markets of Damascus, and died in exile at al-Rabadha — alone, exactly as the Prophet had foretold. The book is structured in eight parts and an appendix, tracing Abu Dharr's life from the pre-Islamic Arabian Peninsula through the Meccan period, the years of closeness with the Prophet in Medina, the Tabuk expedition, the confrontation in Damascus, the contested departure from Medina, and the years of silence and death at al-Rabadha. It draws on the classical Islamic biographical tradition in both its Sunni and Shia transmissions — Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabari, al-Dhahabi, Ibn Abd al-Barr, Ibn Hajar, and Bihar al-Anwar among others — and presents multiple historical readings of contested events without adjudicating between them. The work is written in a hybrid method: documented historical narrative, acknowledged narrative reconstruction, and authorial reflection are distinguished and labelled throughout. It is addressed to the general reader as well as to students of early Islamic history, and to anyone concerned with the enduring tension between truth, power, and conscience. Generative AI tools were used in the drafting, editing, and editorial audit of this work. Full disclosure is provided in the front matter of the book.

summary: This repository accompanies the manuscript Agent-Based Modeling in Tairona Chiefdoms of the Río Frío Basin, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia (c. AD 100 to 1600) and contains the reproducible computational workflow used to construct, calibrate, execute, and evaluate a spatially explicit household agent-based model for the 52.2 km² Río Frío archaeological survey area. The model contrasts bottom-up, mixed, and top-down organizational scenarios while incorporating household production, residential mobility, demographic fission, cooperation, surplus transfer, soil degradation and recovery, ecological forcing, and cumulative landscape investment. Archaeological settlement observations are translated into 25 m cells nested within 250 m analytical zones, and model evaluation follows a pattern-oriented framework comparing observed and simulated change in occupied-zone density, settlement concentration, spatial extent, and nearest-neighbor spacing. The experimental design combines three organizational scenarios with stable, declining, and shock ecological conditions and independently varies landscape investment, producing 360 baseline simulations. Global sensitivity analysis additionally evaluates 16 parameters across 180 Latin hypercube sets. The repository provides the R workflow used for data preparation, simulation, validation, sensitivity analysis, figure generation, and manuscript tables, supporting transparent replication, methodological evaluation, comparative reuse in archaeological modeling, and facilitating critical assessment of alternative mechanisms underlying long-term settlement and socio-ecological change patterns.

summary: A Universal Holder Bound (Abstract) The paper develops a rigorous discrete geometric framework in which gravitational metrics can emerge from fiber-bundle data, affine holonomy, and mapping-tori constructions on discrete spatial geometries. Its core result is a generalized transport-equivariant idempotent-collapse theorem (involving finite Galois descent and conditions ensuring parallel transport preserves image-kernel splittings). Combined with the associated universal Hölder bound on idempotent fiber endomorphisms (verified computationally via exact rational arithmetic on projector matrices across dimensions and ranks), this supplies controlled continuum limits. Core Mechanism and Link to Emergent Gravity Emergent-gravity programs treat geometry and the Einstein equations as effective descriptions arising from more primitive, non-gravitational degrees of freedom (e.g., entanglement, causal sets, information metrics, or discrete spectral data).   Here the primitives are: Strict fiber-bundle formulations over discrete bases. Generalized affine mapping tori (suspensions of affine maps that encode discrete holonomy and monodromy). Idempotent endomorphisms (F) satisfying \(F^2 = F\) whose powers collapse (\(F^{x^2} = F\)) under transport-equivariant conditions. The theorem guarantees that parallel transport along discrete paths preserves the relevant splittings. This allows consistent projection (“collapse”) of the discrete fiber data onto an effective continuum metric. The Hölder bound then supplies a uniform control on the regularity of that metric: curvature (and related quantities) cannot change arbitrarily rapidly. In the language of physics, this bound smoothes classical singularities into finite but highly compressed states. This sits in the same broad family as other discrete-to-continuum approaches (spectral asymptotics of discrete Laplacians recovering the Einstein–Hilbert term, causal-set information geometry, or self-fiber constructions in which geometry is a section of a bundle of metrics).  My related work already derives continuum Riemannian geometry and gravitational dynamics from finite discrete spectral/bundle data on simplicial complexes, with the heat-trace coefficient \(a_2\) fixing an effective Newton constant. The present paper supplies the stricter algebraic and transport-theoretic scaffolding needed for the metric itself to emerge cleanly. Concrete Implications Singularity resolution and UV completeness. A universal Hölder condition on the emergent metric prevents curvature blow-ups. Black-hole and cosmological singularities are replaced by finite-density cores; the same bound is invoked for global regularity questions (e.g., Navier–Stokes) and for taming QFT infinities. Whether the bound is strong enough under the dynamical evolution of the discrete system remains an open physical question, but the mathematical control is explicit. Ontology inversion. Discrete fiber-bundle and Galois data are primary; continuum geometry and gravity are derived, provable consequences. This matches the program’s stated goal of inverting the usual continuum-first ontology. Constraints on corrections. Because the continuum limit is obtained under precise equivariance and descent hypotheses, higher-curvature or non-local corrections are not free parameters; they are correlated with the underlying Cartan/affine and representation data (as already emphasized in the related spectral papers). Testability. The discrete structures are in principle realizable across broad arrays of classical CPUs or near-term quantum simulators (spectral-gap shifts, continuous-time quantum-walk interference, holonomy measurements). Related manuscripts in my Zenodo record already outline measurement protocols and sample-size estimates. Compatibility with other emergent pictures. Affine mapping tori naturally incorporate discrete monodromy; the transport-equivariant projectors resemble the project
title: A Universal Hölder Bound: Infinite Scale Transport

summary: In (1), we introduced a stability method which demonstrates that the Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) and Tsallis distributions are both stable equilibrium solutions linked to the constraints Sum over i p(ei)=1 and Sum over i ei p(ei)= Eave. In (2), which was presented in 2004, a similar association of the MB and Tsallis distributions is presented, based on statistical mechanical considerations of a reservoir. This association is linked with extracting a system from a reservoir. Consider the textbook case of a large reservoir with energy E which has a tiny energy E1 removed. The number of states  w(E-E1) = w(E) - E1 dw/dE = w(E) (1-E1 d/dE ln(w(E) ) approx=  w(E) exp(-E/T) where 1/T = d/dE ln(w(E)). In (2), this equation is presented in the following manner:  w(E-E1) = exp { ln( w(E-E1)) ) = exp{ ln(w(E))-E1 d/dE ln(w(E) } = w(E) exp(-E/T). In other words, (2) presents a function and its inverse, here exp and ln. (2) then suggests writing E-E1 =  E-E* -(E1-E*) and considering a more general function and its inverse. (2) shows that in such a case, the Tsallis distribution arises naturally. Depending on E-E1 or E-E1-(E1-E*), one obtains either the MB or Tsallis distribution.The approach of (2) associates both the MB and Tsallis distributions as does the stability method of (1) and so we wish to point that there exists in the literature a statistical method other than the stability method which suggests that both the MB and Tsallis naturally arise in a similar manner. We stress this association because historically only the MB distribution was considered as an equilibrium solution.
title: Stability Method Yielding Both the Maxwell-Boltzmann and Tsallis Distributions and a Reservoir Method Yielding the Same

summary: Code, synthetic training data and trained models for "Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints" (Bao, Coulson, Valencic, Mousavi, Dangendorf, Lloyd and Mitrovica, submitted to AGU Advances). The direct iterative Fourier neural operator (DIFNO) maps fields between disjoint scattered point sets using direct spectral evaluation with precomputed Vandermonde matrices. A forward DIFNO emulates the elastic sea level equation (Greenland ice-thickness change to sea surface height, SSH, rate), and a physics-informed inverse DIFNO maps SSH back to ice change, constrained by a cycle-consistency loss through the frozen forward model. Files DIFNO-Greenland_code.zip: Jupyter notebooks for training the forward (01_train_forward.ipynb) and inverse (02_train_inverse.ipynb) models, and the model, loss and gradient-surgery source code (src/). Same as the GitHub repository https://github.com/xiyuanbao/DIFNO-Greenland at release time. Requirements are listed in requirements.txt. DIFNO-Greenland_data_*.zip and DIFNO-Greenland_model_*.zip: the data and trained models, split into seven archives of about 350 MB each. Unzip all of them next to the notebooks (unzip '*.zip'); together they form one folder, DIFNO-Greenland_data/, containing - no_smooth/: three synthetic ensembles (single, multi and coastal ice-change families), 10,000 samples each, with ice-thickness change rate at 4,252 Greenland points and the corresponding SSH rate at 4,968 ocean points (m/yr), computed with the sea level equation at spherical harmonic degree 512; - 512full_ref_Gr_case.npz: the reference case, ice-thickness change rate from Simonsen et al. (2021, doi:10.1029/2020GL091216) and its SSH fingerprint on the same points; - 512Gr_oc_coords_full.npz and 512scaled_display_coords_full.pt: point coordinates in longitude and latitude, and in the scaled polar stereographic coordinates used by the models; - _Models/: the four trained models used in the paper (default and coastal forward, default and coastal inverse). README_data.md (in DIFNO-Greenland_data_coastal_coords_ref.zip) describes each file, array shape and unit.
title: Code, training data and model checkpoints for DIFNO-Greenland

summary: Version 2. Version 1 archived the 2026-09-22 extract and a 2026-09-27 snapshot for isoniazid and rifampin. Version 2 documents an error in the 2026-09-22 extract, adds bedaquiline, clofazimine, delamanid and linezolid to both sets, and adds a script that reproduces the finding. The error. In every amr_*_full.csv file of the 2026-09-22 extract, genome_id was stored as a number, which drops trailing zeros (1733.9420 becomes 1733.942). The shortened identifier is usually that of a different, real genome, so about 10% of records were attached to the wrong genome. The isoniazid and rifampin files also lack about 6,800 laboratory records each, almost all citing PMID 30280646. This is an error in how the authors produced the extract; there is no evidence of any change to BV-BRC. After the same number conversion is applied to the 2026-09-27 identifiers, every record in the 2026-09-22 files, for all six drugs and both evidence types, is found in the 2026-09-27 snapshot. Consequences for the audit built on the extract. 3,114 of 31,664 isoniazid and rifampin laboratory records (9.8%) belong to another genome. Of 747 genome×drug groups carrying both a Resistant and a Susceptible laboratory record, 668 were created by records of another genome; the complete snapshot has 88, all isoniazid pairs at 0.1 (Resistant) and 0.4 (Susceptible). All 76 records classed as confirmed discrepancies, and all 754 laboratory records of the 399-genome 'orphan batch', belong to other genomes. Contents. frozen_extract_2026-09-22/ : the extract as analysed, unchanged and including the error, for six drugs, with genome metadata. pre_reply_snapshot_2026-09-27/ : every genome_amr record for the six drugs across all taxa, with all API fields including record identifiers and insertion/modification dates (row counts equal the API totals), genome metadata, pull scripts and manifests. The snapshot was taken on 2026-09-27, the day the authors sent factual-verification requests to the maintainers of BV-BRC, the CRyPTIC Consortium Dataset and the Hu et al. (2024) AMR benchmark. integrity_check_2026-09-27/ : check_extract.py, its outputs, and the audit objects it traces. The 2026-09-22 files are kept only so that the audit and the check can be reproduced; do not use them as a copy of BV-BRC. SHA256SUMS.txt gives a SHA-256 checksum for every other file. Zenodo stores files without folders, so each file name carries its folder as a prefix (folder__file); restore the folders before running the scripts.

summary: This video shows the sequential three-dimensional reconstruction of the vicinome of a single dendritic spine, the full set of neuronal and glial elements that surround it, in the human cerebral cortex. The spine belongs to a layer 5 pyramidal neuron and was reconstructed from the H01 petavoxel dataset, one cubic millimeter of human temporal cortex imaged at nanometer resolution and navigated through Neuroglancer. The sequence begins with the spine alone and adds one neighboring element at a time, so that a structure that first appears isolated is revealed, frame by frame, as a hub embedded in dense neuropil. Each frame lasts one second and the final frame is held to show the complete neighborhood. This material accompanies the manuscript "The dendritic spine vicinome: characterizing its crowding in the human brain with petavoxel electron microscopy" (Manjarrez, Lozada, Zamora-Ursulo, and Flores).
title: The dendritic spine vicinome: a 3D video of a spine and its neighboring elements in human cortex

summary: This package contains the data and the code that reproduce every table, figure and number reported in the article. A single script ( run_all.sh ) runs all steps in about 25 seconds and ends by checking that each generated output is byte-for-byte identical to the one used in the manuscript. What the paper does. Spanish households increasingly buy their food with the preparation already done. The paper measures this with an ordinal index of Domestic Labour Substitution (DLS) built on eleven "ladders" — market forms of the same food, ordered by the amount of household preparation they displace to the market — and asks whether the shift reflects the rising value of household time or the falling relative price of processed food. A conditional-logit model of the choice among forms implies that a price change common to all households cancels, to first order, in the gap between household groups shopping in the same market, which directs the test to the COVID-19 lockdown as a shock to the relative value of time. Contents. data/raw/mapa/ — the 14 annual files of the Spanish household food consumption panel ( Panel de Consumo Alimentario en los Hogares , MAPA), 2014–2025, unaltered, with a manifest listing the source URL, size and SHA-256 checksum of each file. data/raw/eurostat/ — snapshots of the Eurostat series used: regional employment rates ( lfst_r_lfe2emprt ), national employment and participation rates ( lfsi_emp_a ) and time use by labour status ( tus_00selfstat ), each with its query URLs. code/ — numbered scripts: extraction of the ladders, recovery of the population behind each published household segment, time-use figures, all estimates and tests, the figure, and a final byte-for-byte check against the reference outputs. Optional scripts re-download the source data and verify the checksums. reference/ — the tables and numbers as published in the article. README.md — data provenance and licensing, computational requirements, description of each program, and the mapping from each table, figure and in-text number to the script that produces it, following the Social Science Data Editors template. Requirements. Python 3.11 with numpy, openpyxl and matplotlib ( requirements.txt ). The random seed is fixed, so the wild cluster bootstrap p-values reproduce exactly. Data sources and terms. MAPA data are reproduced unaltered under the reuse terms of the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (the source must be cited and the update metadata preserved; Ley 37/2007). Eurostat data are reused under CC BY 4.0 (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU). The code is released under the MIT License (see LICENSE ). Related article. Recio-Román, A., Recio-Menéndez, M., & Román-González, M. V. (2026). Who Cooks When the Supermarket Cooks? The Value of Time and the Market Substitution of Domestic Food Preparation in Spain. Manuscript submitted for publication.

summary: A database of atomic layer deposition (ALD) process parameters extracted from the full text of the scientific literature by an open-weight large language model, together with the manually annotated gold standards used to validate the extraction and a provenance table linking each value to a character span in its own source article. From 11,988 records returned by four rounds of Scopus keyword searches (11,892 after de-duplication), the full text of 1,706 articles was retrieved and parsed; 640 of these never mention atomic layer deposition in their own text and were excluded, and 16 were set aside as in-context demonstrations. Eight process parameters (deposited material, precursor, co-reactant, deposition temperature, growth per cycle, chamber pressure, pulse time and purge time) were extracted from the remaining 1,050 articles, of which 597 yielded at least one value, giving 3,884 article-field rows. summary: Abstract: Infectious disease transmission involves interactions occurring at multiple organizational levels, including individuals, households, communities, and regions. Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. Keywords: SuperHyperGraph; hypergraph neural networks; hierarchical epidemic modeling; higher order interactions; SEIR dynamics; source identification; environmental perturbations; Lipschitz stability —————————————————————————————————————————-
title: Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Networks for Hierarchical Epidemic Modeling, Environmental Perturbations, and Source Identifiability

summary: A thirteen-chapter monograph on geometric and analytic structures that recur in quantum gravity. The chapters range from functional realizations of matrices and tensors to emergent spacetime. Each chapter separates proved results from conjectures and heuristic proposals, and states that status explicitly. Part I (Ch. 1–2) studies functional realizations of matrices and tensors and geometric flows on matrix, tensor and graphon spaces. Part II (Ch. 3–6) covers: - the analytic continuation of Pascal's simplex; - Beta-kernel operators; - interdimensional transforms; - analysis on Sierpiński simplices. Proved results in Part II include: - the asymptotics of continuous multinomial integrals; - an expansion of the continuous row entropy via the Barnes G-function; - an inversion formula for the Radon–Beta transform. Part III (Ch. 7–10) develops the L∞ minimax extrinsic-curvature problem for submanifolds and curves in obstacle domains. Its proved results include: - existence for curves; - a contact principle; - sharp U-turn bounds in Euclidean and constant-curvature spaces; - finiteness of homotopy classes under a length bound. Part III also treats applications to ADM slicings and relativistic trajectories. It shows the limits of transferring the problem to information geometry. Part IV (Ch. 11–12) reviews established links between entanglement, tensor networks and gravity, with sources (linearized Einstein equations from the entanglement first law, min-cut bounds, the loop-quantum-gravity area spectrum). It formulates the open questions as conjectures. Part V (Ch. 13) is an order-of-magnitude assessment. It concludes that Planck-suppressed signatures of the two-scale spectral-dimension model lie far below current and planned sensitivities. The Lean 4 files in the companion repository are a naming skeleton and do not verify the mathematics. LaTeX sources, numerical checks, audit records and the register of findings are in the repository: https://github.com/reinaldomsilvafilho-netizen/quantum-gravity-lean4
title: Geometry, Tensors, and Quantum Gravity

summary: When should a firm deploy a fixed amount of implementation capacity over time? This paper shows that the technically efficient timing of implementation can differ from the strategically optimal timing when implementation affects future competitive-state transitions. Two implementations may generate identical current actions and payoffs while inducing different future transition probabilities, so current- action equivalence need not imply dynamic equivalence. We model a scarce implementation capacity whose temporal allocation affects a cumulative transition index and derive the resulting strategic alloca- tion. The main result provides a necessary-and-sufficient condition for technical and strategic allocations to coincide: marginal transition productivity must be constant across dates at the technical allocation. When it is heterogeneous, strategic value reallocates capacity toward dates with higher marginal tran- sition productivity. A local characterization shows that the magnitude of this distortion increases with the strategic stake and transition heterogeneity, while decreasing with the curvature of the implementa- tion loss and with transition saturation. A two-window specialization yields a sharp economic signature: sufficiently large strategic stakes can reverse the technically preferred timing of implementation. The analysis identifies a timing margin distinct from information acquisition and standard capacity invest- ment by showing that implementation itself can change the future transition technology even when current actions and payoffs are unchanged
title: Strategic Timing of Implementation and Future-State Transition

Rocaille, a characteristic ornament of the period, exhibits a continuously transforming morphology that has historically resisted systematic formal description. The dataset comprises 1,611 high-resolution digitizations from major German collections, accompanied by expert-curated bilingual metadata and commentary describing iconography and ornamental morphology. A subset of 229 images includes pixel-accurate segmentation masks distinguishing the structural volutes and comb-like extensions of the Rocaille. The images, structured metadata, textual descriptions, and segmentation annotations together support computational analyses ranging from visual multimodal retrieval and semantic segmentation to morphological analysis. As technical validation, we train two standard vision backbones for segmentation, showing that the annotations provide a learnable segmentation signal and that pre-training on both external and on our dataset can support downstream learning. summary: This paper develops a preliminary account of normative formation under conditions in which heterogeneous sources possess unequal capacities to generate, stabilize, interpret, circulate, and revise normative structures. Normative formation is used broadly for the emergence of relatively stable concepts, evaluative distinctions, interpretive conventions, practical expectations, and recognized modes of reasoning and action; normative grammar serves only as an analytical analogy for partially stabilized relations among them. The central concern is relational and temporal. Differences in generative capacity may affect the relative influence of normative sources and, under some conditions, the later conditions through which other sources can participate in formation. The paper therefore distinguishes generative capacity from realized normative influence and develops the provisional concepts of endogenous weighting, generative crowding-out, and normative closure. Three case studies refine the framework from different directions: philosophical claim formation foregrounds argumentative provenance; international law foregrounds practice, identification, interpretation, and legally relevant history; aesthetic norm formation foregrounds pre-explicit differentiation and the possible co-formation of judgment and norm. The later analysis develops a trajectory-sensitive perspective in which the significance of asymmetry depends partly on its provenance, persistence, revisability, self-reinforcement, and effects on future generative capacities. The discussion remains exploratory and offers neither a complete theory of normativity or power nor a general metric of justice or institutional design.
title: A Preliminary Discussion of Normative Formation under Asymmetric Generative Capacity

summary: Learned and search-based docking are often compared on the top-ranked pose alone. On 303 benchmark complexes, each ligand was docked against its whole receptor with three configured pipelines, namely AutoDock Vina with gnina rescoring (AutoDock), the diffusion model DiffDock-L with smina optimisation (DiffDock) and EquiBind with gnina optimisation (EquiBind). No pipeline received binding-site information. A qualifying pose was PoseBusters-valid and within 2 angstroms root-mean-square deviation of the nearest deposited ligand copy, and up to thirty ranked poses were scored per complex. Raw learned poses were largely invalid, at 24.4% pooled validity for DiffDock and 2.9% for EquiBind against 99.6% for AutoDock Vina. Local optimisation repaired validity but recovered no grossly misplaced binding mode. Rank-1 recovery was 49.2% for AutoDock, 43.6% for DiffDock and 18.8% for EquiBind. The AutoDock figure rests on gnina re-ranking, because Vina's own order reached 42.9%. At 2 angstroms the leading pair was not separated at rank-1 (95% interval -1.7 to +12.8 points), whereas at 1 angstrom it was. Retrospective best-of-top-15 recovery reached 70.3% for AutoDock and 59.1% for DiffDock, a resolved gap conditional on search effort and receptor preparation. Six to seven in ten leading-pair rank-1 failures held no qualifying pose in the ranked pool. Better ranking cannot repair such failures. Charged cost per qualifying pose did not separate AutoDock and DiffDock, although per solved complex AutoDock was cheaper. A reference-free Orai1 demonstration illustrates the validity and placement screens. Variants were selected on the same benchmark, and the comparison describes these pipelines and hardware, not method classes.
title: Beyond the Top-Ranked Pose: Validity, Ranking Depth and Cost in Blind Docking

summary: For each ordering of the vertices of a finite simple graph, record the number of previously revealed neighbors at each step. The vertex-exposure enumerator records the distribution of these words over all vertex orderings. We prove that it distinguishes all finite trees up to isomorphism. After word reversal, this enumerator is the rank-sequence G-invariant of the graph's coverage polymatroid. The proof combines shuffle multiplication and edge deletion with weighted leaf-core extraction, Lie-cobracket pruning, and centroid rigidity. We also define a rooted cut law and prove that it distinguishes rooted trees and rooted connected unicyclic graphs. For connected unicyclic graphs, the vertex-exposure enumerator determines the cycle length and the multiset of rooted trees attached to the cycle. It determines such a graph among all finite simple graphs when the cycle is a triangle or the maximum degree is attained at a unique vertex. On connected unicyclic graphs, it strictly refines both the full U-polynomial and the chromatic symmetric function. Finally, an explicit finite relation rules out a uniform rational linear specialization from the vertex-exposure enumerator to the chromatic symmetric function on all finite simple graphs. Completeness of the enumerator for general finite simple graphs remains open.
title: Vertex-exposure words distinguish all trees

summary: Restricted response equivalence does not determine the response to a different source or the output of a different observation. We study this distinction in two linked, explicitly specified superconducting model comparisons. A conserving, particle–hole-symmetric density model gives identical linear responses for a two-point form factor and a smooth angular form factor with the same first two moments. Its diagonal cubic response contains the fourth moment. A supplied additional singlet channel modifies that dependence, and a smooth family approaching the two-point distribution eliminates a uniform cubic-coefficient separation on bounded, pole-separated domains. We then turn to distinct finite-energy optical completions, retaining their actual dispersion, pairing regulator, gap feedback, occupied-sea currents, and electromagnetic attachment. Their lower optical responses can already differ; seventh order is not asserted to be the first optical discriminator. For a fixed two-tone, same-incident-field comparison, inherited computer-assisted continuum enclosures certify a nonzero selected seventh-degree coefficient, two ninth-degree corrections, and an all-order remainder. The resulting relative-error bounds hold at explicitly very small normalized amplitudes and do not establish practical detectability. Finally, we distinguish phase selection from square-law detection and state the waveform and preparation conditions under which a sign-reversal pilot estimator preserves a finite linear query. The result is a model-specific, source-explicit comparison with auditable error accounting, not universal band identification or a derivation of the superconducting interaction from complementarity. The supplement contains the declared model/proof notes, curated numerical source and inputs, all seven accuracy cases, historical failure and replay records, and the accepted repaired Lean source with statement/axiom evidence and correspondence. The completed local Lean review covers 57 selected theorem declarations and ten supporting definitions/types. It is not a formalization of the entire microscopic derivation, continuum-enclosure producer, all-order tail, or physical detector preparation. A final separately organized AI-assisted technical review repeated the original saved-endpoint checks; it was not an independent external referee review. Mathematical accuracy at very small normalized amplitudes is not demonstrated experimental sensitivity.
tags: conserving density response; nonlinear superconducting response; continuum enclosure; phase-selected fields; inverse inference; calibrated observation; Lean.
title: From Density-Response Equivalence to Validated Nonlinear Contrast in Superconducting Models
