summary: Neural receivers for 5G NR are commonly compared against least-squares (LS) baselines, which leaves open whether they improve on a well-tuned classical receiver and whether their gains survive conditions outside the training distribution. We evaluate a fully convolutional neural receiver and a lightweight hybrid receiver, which retains a classical LS and linear minimum mean-squared error (LMMSE) front end and learns a residual correction of its log-likelihood ratios, on standard-compliant 5G NR PUSCH with 3GPP tapped delay line channels and hardware impairments. Baselines include an LMMSE channel estimator supplied with the empirical statistics of each test scenario (genie) and one supplied with a single fixed set of statistics from the training mixture (practical). Inside the training range both learned receivers only match the genie baseline. Two regimes differ. With an RMS delay spread of 2000 ns the learned receivers require 0.90 dB less than the genie baseline, while the practical LMMSE receiver does not reach 10 percent BLER at all; with a single DMRS symbol the neural receiver requires 4.08 dB less than the best classical receiver at 20 m/s and is the only receiver that operates at 30 m/s. We further show that the apparent failure of learned receivers outside the training envelope is a matter of training coverage rather than architecture: widening the training delay spread from 30-300 ns to 30-1000 ns converts a 5.97 dB deficit at 2000 ns into a 0.90 dB advantage, at a cost of at most 0.1 dB for speeds up to 45 m/s. Trained on the same range, the hybrid receiver matches the full neural receiver within 0.05 dB using 3.9x fewer parameters and FLOPs. Finally, we document a baseline pitfall: DMRS-based carrier frequency offset compensation also removes the Doppler shift of a dominant line-of-sight path, invalidating the LMMSE correlation model and costing 0.84 dB, which can produce illusory gains for learned receivers. Code, configurations and results: https://github.com/Ewwftyy/neural-receiver-5g-nr
title: Training Coverage, Not Architecture, Decides When Learned 5G NR Receivers Help

summary: The clinical laboratory diagnostic service is the backbone of all medical decisions, but at the health sector the results of laboratory tests for patients are becoming conflicted between various health care sectors in many regions including Kirkuk, Iraq.This diagnostic mismatch jeopardizes timely medical care, imposes a financial burden on twice on patients and significantly undermines public trust of the local health system. This study explores the causes of intra- and inter-laboratory differences, which span the diagnostic testing experience and can be broken down into pre-analytical (60-70% of errors), analytical (10-15%) and post-analytical (15-20%) phases. These inconsistencies undermine patients' trust in healthcare providers and institutions, leading them to view such issues as evidence of systemic healthcare failures. The study identifies and outlines targeted mitigation strategies through analysis of patient preparation, specimen collection and instrument calibration, and data transcription. Solving this health-care problem needs two strategies: First, laboratory staff must follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) with great care, as well as strictly follow the sample rejection criteria, and apply Internal Quality Control (IQC). Second, structural governance of Directorate of Health is required: mandatory ISO 15189 accreditation, centralized External Quality Assessment (EQA) programs, unannounced audits and agreed upon provincial reference intervals are crucial to recon gain patient confidence and obtain diagnostic reliability.
tags: Laboratory diagnostics, specimen collection, health system.
title: Discrepancies in Laboratory Test Results and Their Impact on Patient Confidence in The Health System in Kirkuk, Iraq

summary: Artifact accompanying a manuscript under double-blind review . Author information is withheld until publication; a later version of this record will carry it, and the concept DOI is stable across versions. What this is. When two unlabelled subgroups of documents are compared by embedding similarity across languages, countries, corpora or periods, and the difference is read as evidence about those sources, no accuracy figure certifies that reading. within_language_baseline.py supplies the missing baseline: it measures the same subgroup contrast inside a single source, where no across-source relation can enter, and reports the residual with a bootstrap interval and an equivalence verdict against a margin declared in advance. The tool has no dependency on the accompanying study and runs on any corpus with three columns ( text , group , source ). It carries its own injection tests ( --selftest ). The bootstrap resamples documents rather than pairs and excludes duplicate draws of the same document from within-source pairs. Also included: the 36 frozen anchor correspondences used as the gold standard, the per-encoder CJK retrieval evaluation, the measured within-language and cross-country genre gaps, the equivalence intervals, an append-only correction record for the non-analytic genealogy fields of the frozen anchors, and anonymised review copies of the post hoc centring protocols and of the departure record. MANIFEST.sha256 covers every deposited file except itself.
title: Replication artifact for "Auditing Cross-Lingual Statutory Similarity Contrasts: Centring Choices and Within-Language Baselines"

summary: Conditional mathematical arguments need careful bookkeeping: which obligations were incurred, which have been addressed, and which were addressed in a way that actually proves the target. Audited Operational Realisability (AOR) is a mathematical theory of this bookkeeping. An audit state consists of demanded records and stored certificates; each certificate carries a status, such as budgeted or blocked , and a payload whose meaning is fixed in advance. We separate three conclusions that are easily conflated. Inference closure registers every dependency of a demanded record, accounting requires a stored certificate for each demanded or dependency-reachable record, and delivery requires a certificate whose status an explicit consumer policy accepts as proving its target. A certificate recording that a budget is exceeded accounts for the obligation but does not deliver feasibility to a consumer who requires it. We prove that inference closure is a reflection that creates no evidence, in a category whose arrows preserve certificates exactly, and that this category has colimits in which every accepted certificate is already stored at some object of the diagram. For operations that add evidence, we prove finite completion under a decreasing rank and confluence under replayability, and we strictly separate accounting, recoverability, and uniform quantitative control. Retained evidence passes to increasing unions, and witnesses pass to limits under compactness and closed validity, provided an accepted payload is returned at the limit; without compactness they may escape. Two examples mark the boundary of accounting: a query system that pays its declared costs, is accounted, and identifies each hidden world along its exhaustive run, yet admits no finite-stage guarantee uniform over all worlds; and a Lipschitz target whose shrinking finite-prefix certificates, priced within a summable credit, are all accepted, with centers converging to the target. The stated structural results are formalized in Lean 4; the analytic estimates of applications remain explicit hypotheses.
title: Audited Operational Realisability: Canonical Inference Closure and Evidence-Preserving Composition

summary: Replication package for the paper "Use-dependent depreciation of intangible capital: thresholds, history dependence, and generative artificial intelligence." The paper studies a firm that accumulates an intangible stock — interpreted as the quality of its data estate — while the intensity with which it deploys a generative AI system accelerates the depreciation of that same stock. Optimal deployment therefore carries an intertemporal contamination wedge: the marginal value of scale is reduced by the shadow price of the stock times the marginal contribution of use to its decay. Under an S-shaped effectiveness function the problem admits three steady states, and optimal policy is history-dependent, separated by a threshold in the initial state obtained by value matching rather than by any local property of the unstable equilibrium. This package reproduces every number, table and figure reported in the paper. It contains three Python modules and no data: all results are generated from the model primitives and the stated parameter values. Contents model.py — model primitives and the numerical solver: steady states, stable manifolds, value functions, and the threshold by value matching. run_all.py — driver that reproduces all reported quantities and writes results/all_results.json . Runtime is approximately 25 minutes on a laptop; the Monte Carlo exercises dominate. make_figures.py — regenerates Figures 1 to 5 as PDF from the solver output. README.md — numerical methods, seeds, validation, and the classification scheme for perturbed draws. Requirements Python 3.10 or later with NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib. No other dependencies. Tested on NumPy 2.4, SciPy 1.17 and Matplotlib 3.10. Numerical methods Steady states are the roots of a scalar residual, bracketed on a grid and refined by Brent's method to a tolerance of 1e-13. Stable manifolds are obtained by eigen-decomposing the Jacobian at each saddle point, displacing along the stable eigenvector, and integrating the time-reversed canonical system with an adaptive Runge–Kutta scheme at relative tolerance 1e-11. Value functions exploit the identity between the costate and the derivative of the value function along the optimal path, with the constant of integration fixed by the perpetuity value at the steady state; this avoids forward integration, which is unstable off the saddle path. The threshold solves the value-matching condition on the overlap of the two manifold domains. Reproducibility All stochastic exercises use a fixed seed, numpy.random.default_rng(20260731) , so re-running reproduces the reported frequencies exactly. The shape of the effectiveness function is a parameter of the model rather than a code branch, so the exercises that compare specifications require no modification of the solver. Validation Value functions are cross-validated against direct time integration of discounted profit along the manifolds; the two computations agree to relative errors of 2.4e-6 and 6.2e-6 on the low and high branches. Single crossing of the difference of the two value functions is not established analytically, so the package records, for every perturbed draw admitting a threshold, whether that difference is strictly monotone on a 400-point grid. Draws on which the solver fails are reported as errors rather than discarded silently. Citation Please cite both this software and the associated paper. A CITATION.cff file is included.
title: Replication Package for: Use-dependent depreciation of intangible capital: thresholds, history dependence, and generative artificial intelligence

summary: A systematic framework for quantum algorithm development covering 20 scientific problem domains with standardized maturity gates, automated validation, resource estimation pipelines, and Azure Quantum integration. Problems are held to explicit maturity gates rather than assumed to pass them: 9 problems are at Stage C, 8 remain at Stage B, and 3 have reached Stage D. All 20 have real Azure Quantum Resource Estimator profiles (1,746 to 754,715 physical qubits), and all 20 calibration ensembles carry valid statistics bound to hashes of the Q# sources they ran. No problem currently demonstrates quantum advantage on available hardware, and 11 of the 20 were downgraded on I/O bottlenecks, quadratic-only speedups or no proven speedup. Implements 10 algorithm families (VQE, QAOA, Grover, HHL, Shor, amplitude estimation, swap test, QEC, quantum walk, Trotter simulation) using the modern Microsoft QDK (qsharp 1.31.0, no .NET dependency); the hardware kernels of the five VQE problems have since been replaced by quantum phase estimation. Also includes a deployed evaluation service that routes a natural-language problem description to one of four verdicts using a deterministic rule set rather than model judgement, a paper classifier measured for over-claim rate against a labelled corpus, and generated Q# that is compiled and resource-estimated before it is reported. Includes cross-problem comparison dashboard, per-problem detail pages with charts, and embedded README documentation.
title: Quantum Grand Challenges: Systematic Quantum Algorithm Development Across 20 Application Domains

summary: Background: Traditional post-marketing drug monitoring framework metrics rely heavily upon passive, spontaneous clinical case notification configurations. These configurations systematically suffer from extensive reporting lag phases and a massive underreporting of actual consumer adverse drug reactions (ADRs). With the explosive expansion of global digital platforms, modern patient networks frequently document raw, unformatted clinical complaints online long before consulting a healthcare practitioner. Objective: This core research constructs, validates, and evaluates an enterprise cloud architecture prototype termed "Shreyas SmartPV Mobile" to automate case intake pipelines, deploy cognitive semantic extractors, map raw text onto official MedDRA hierarchies, and execute immediate regulatory eligibility checks. Methodology: A multi-layered low-code pipeline structure was engineered using Glide Apps and Softr for responsive frontend client interface extraction, Airtable as the primary secure relational cloud database storage, and Make.com as the background workflow synchronization integration orchestrator. Data streams are processed via a cognitive node driven by the Google Gemini Large Language Model (LLM) framework running specific clinical validation rules, multi-stage Named Entity Recognition (NER), and automated token dictionaries to extract suspect therapeutic drug classes cleanly from descriptive toxicological events. Results: Extensive experimental validation using standard chemical benchmark metrics (including Paracetamol, Aspirin, and Ibuprofen scenarios) verified 100% precision in parsing unstructured digital narratives, mapping baseline complaints to standard MedDRA Preferred Terms (PT) (e.g., matching 'red rashes on skin' to Erythematous Rash), and computing immediate validation states (Report Valid? = True) based on strict international safety compliance requirements. The system recorded an average automated triage execution velocity of less than 3.9 seconds per array. Conclusion: The validated automation workflow confirms that cloud-native cognitive processing pipelines cut manual data entry fatigue, optimize processing costs, and maximize patient-reported signal capture. This technical transition shifts drug safety management from passive tracking arrays into dynamic, real-time digital active safety listening ecosystems.
tags: Pharmacovigilance, Artificial Intelligence, MedDRA Ontology, Cloud Orchestration, Large Language Models, Low-Code Systems Engineering
title: AI-Driven Social Media Listening And Automated Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) Extraction System For Advanced Pharmacovigilance

summary: Abstract: A geometric construction of inverse-square gravity is presented in which solid angle accounts only for spatial dilution, while universal coupling to mass-energy supplies the physical strength of the interaction. This separation avoids treating a body-dependent geometric parameter as a substitute for gravitational mass. For a static spherical source, the construction recovers the exterior Newtonian potential per unit test mass, Φ(r) = -GM/r. Combining this static scalar potential with the special-relativistic energy of the escaping particle gives:   v_esc(r) = c * sqrt( 1 - 1 / (1 + GM / (r * c^2))^2 ) The result is subluminal for all finite r and reduces to the Newtonian escape velocity in the weak-field limit. The model is not presented as a replacement for general relativity, nor as a complete Lorentz-covariant field theory. Rather, it is a flat-spacetime scalar-potential construction that clarifies what follows from solid-angle dilution, universal mass coupling, and special-relativistic energy conservation before additional assumptions, such as wave propagation or optical-gravity extensions, are introduced.   Note on Versioning & Relationship to Prior Work: This paper presents a standalone, refined mathematical derivation focusing specifically on the static scalar formulation and relativistic escape condition. It serves as an independent baseline related to the foundational concepts outlined in the author's broader work ( A Solid-Angle Postulate as a Geometric Foundation for Gravity , DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19333670).
tags: gravitation; solid angle; inverse-square law; Newtonian potential; universal mass coupling; escape velocity; special relativity; scalar potential; flat spacetime; wave-optical gravity
title: Solid-Angle Dilution and Relativistic Escape Velocity

summary: International Environmental Law stands at a crossroad, where its basic ideas and principles are massively coming at odds with the depth and demand of universal environmental catastrophe. Greatly based upon notions of state control, assent, and fragmented international agreement, the discipline has failed to respond to massive environmental degradation and biodiversity failure. The formation of the scientific notion of the ecological boundaries and limits has elevated the constraint by introducing a bunch of environmental thresholds and limits within which the humankind can remain secure. Developed by the Stockholm Resilience Centre, this framework uncovers crucial biodiversity dynamics like the massive ecological destruction, ecological threshold, poor land usage and change, and bio-geochemical cycles and hence introduces a novice standard beyond which the irreparable environmental damage sharply increases and spikes. While this model has gained impeccable speed and admiration among scientific and policy stakeholders, its ethical interpretation and application for international law remains questionable. This paper argues that adopting environmental limits within the scope and ambit of international environmental law calls for a thorough transformation from fragmented governance towards an obligatory structure of earth system governance.
title: Planetary Boundaries And International Environmental Law: Towards Earth System Governance

summary: On a supplied real Euclidean two-plane, admitting both rotations and reflections gives the transport group O(2) = U(1) ⋊ Z₂, not an untwisted circle. We organize the resulting graph, face, refinement, and readout structures in one assumption-controlled framework. On a connected finite graph, tree gauge reduces the edge data to a simultaneous conjugacy class of free generators. Its determinant class lies in H¹(Γ; Z₂), while the phase is a crossed cocycle for the associated sign action. Admitting faces introduces additional path comparisons: their determinant defects obey a relative boundary law, and a rooted tetrahedral word gives an exact non-Abelian Bianchi identity whose phase sum is sign-twisted. Shared-edge and common-root data permit exact boundary cancellation under the stated disk refinements. Explicit pentagonal and hexagonal certificates include all five and fourteen triangulations, respectively, and two mixed 1–3, 2–2, 3–1 routes. Mismatched-edge and omitted-root controls distinguish invalid fusion, while a preserved reverse-order null control shows why equality of evaluated matrices is weaker than equality of free boundary words. A locally flat annulus retains a nontrivial noncontractible reflection holonomy. Finally, conjugacy data, one prepared direction, a complete endpoint frame, and a separately supplied complex-linear process representation have different identification power. The component graph-gauge, cohomological, lattice-Bianchi, and triangulation structures have established antecedents. The proposed contribution is their explicit finite integration with typed root, edge-sharing, and access contracts. No arbitrary-mesh or continuum invariance, higher gauge theory, quantum-state selection, winding lift, probability law, or empirical realization follows from the construction.
tags: complementarity; O(2) holonomy; twisted cohomology; finite cell complexes; Bianchi identity; boundary parity; refinement; reference frames; Lean.
title: Twisted O(2) Holonomy on Finite Cell Complexes: Cohomology, Bianchi Closure, and Refinement

summary: Conventional black-box predictive models consistently exhaust the limited memory boundaries of industrial edge microcontrollers. Massive parameter footprints and opaque decision pathways render standard neural networks highly vulnerable to out-of-distribution catastrophic failures. The proposed physics-informed symbolic artificial intelligence architecture formulates transparent degradation equations tailored directly to individual hardware characteristics. An autonomous generator fuses fundamental electrical constraints with a localized polynomial expansion to produce extreme low-dimensional operational logic. Empirical evaluations utilizing the NASA Ames repository demonstrate the absolute elimination of cross-run extrapolation errors. The customized equations require a strict maximum footprint of 140 Bytes and execute at a constant O(1) inference complexity. The explicit physical formulation reduces total execution energy consumption by a factor of 2.8 compared to baseline multi-layer perceptrons, while maintaining a 0.9994 accuracy score under severe data scarcity. Synthetic noise injection tests confirm supreme operational resilience against severe sensor distortions. Absolute white-box interpretability provides field engineers with the direct capability to audit the precise prognostic logic prior to chip deployment. The decentralized deployment of deterministic diagnostic intelligence establishes a highly robust foundation for sustainable smart manufacturing ecosystems.
title: Physics-Informed Symbolic AI: An Explainable Edge-Native Framework for Industrial Prognostics

summary: This dataset provides the nationally consistent, footprint-level classification of residential building subtypes across the United States. It contains over 140 million building footprints classified into four distinct structural residential categories:  Single-Family Homes (SFHs), Townhouses (including duplexes), Apartments, and Mobile Homes .    The dataset is organized geographically and stored as individual, high-performance GeoPackage ( .gpkg ) files for each of the 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia .   Data Schema (Attribute Fields) Each state-level GeoPackage contains the following standardized attribute columns:   geometry (Polygon) : The spatial boundary (polygon) of the building footprint. Res_type (Integer) : The classified residential structural subtype code: 1 = Single-Family Home (SFH) 2 = Townhouse (explicitly includes laterally attached row houses and semi-detached duplexes) 3 = Apartment 4 = Mobile Home height (Double) : The estimated physical height of the building in meters. Baseline heights are obtained from Microsoft Global ML footprints, with a minimum threshold of 4.2 m enforced (representing a typical one-story structure) and missing values imputed using local tract-level medians. type (String) : Building type tags from OSM building footprint (Limited coverage and varies by region).   Methodology and Classification Workflow The residential classifications were achieved using a novel, scalable hierarchical spatial workflow that integrates geometric building footprints with high-confidence administrative and demographic auxiliary data:   Multi-Source Footprint Integration: Geometry was compiled by merging Microsoft US Building Footprints, Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, and OpenStreetMap (OSM) geometries. Non-residential structures were purged during preprocessing using OSM land-use layers and manual reclassification of OSM building tags. Mobile Home Identification: Candidate footprints located within spatial buffers around documented mobile home parks were classified using state-specific Random Forest (RF) models trained on footprint geometry (area, aspect ratio, rectangularity, and local density). High-confidence "seeds" were subsequently expanded using context-aware spatial promotion rules. Single-Family Home (SFH) Calibration: High-confidence SFHs were initially mapped using administrative address attributes. To prevent over- or under-counting, a size-ranked rule-based spatial promotion algorithm was implemented to sequentially classify candidate footprints until the counts aligned with rigorous state-level housing stock benchmarks derived from the American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates. Townhouse and Apartment Discrimination: The remaining unclassified structures were categorized using a sequential, rule-based physical geometry and address-point pattern-recognition workflow. Duplexes and linear townhouses were distinguished from multi-family apartment blocks by evaluating physical constraints (convexity, height, and structural width) paired with the spatial density and linear alignment of internal address points from the National Address Database (NAD) . Spatial Context Completion: A final, iterative morphological distance-matching algorithm resolved any remaining unclassified structures based on local neighborhood class composition and physical architectural similarities (height, area, and aspect ratio).
title: Nationwide Footprint-Level Classification of Residential Building Subtypes for the United States

summary: Contactless palmprint recognition is attractive for mobile biometrics, yet how well a learned representation transfers between acquisition settings is rarely measured. Using CompNet - a compact network of learnable Gabor filters and competitive coding — we apply one unified protocol to two contrasting databases: the constrained near-infrared IITD and the unconstrained smartphone SMPD. Within each, CompNet reaches 98.70% Rank-1 accuracy at an equal-error rate below 1.4%. Across databases the transfer is asymmetric: mobile-trained features generalize to controlled data (91.10%), whereas the reverse collapses (40.03%), so generalization flows from harder to easier domains.
title: Contactless palmprint identification using CompNet on the IITD and SMPD databases

summary: One cumulative programme, one canonical DOI. This edition reunites the original collection and all material previously issued in a separate continuation. The permanent project DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.22678085 . All earlier mathematical files, complete LaTeX, human citations and source archives are retained. Selected main papers remain separately readable; the full set of 98 original PDFs is also preserved in one ZIP. This is a publication consolidation, not a new proof or a change to the mathematical scope. Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme is a cumulative collection of mathematical papers, complete LaTeX proofs, formalization sources, calculations and literature-based research notes. Its central question is how the zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be studied through explicitly constructed arithmetic cohomology, spectral actions and quantitative metric estimates. The collection also retains the related heat-flow, arithmetic-trace, fluid, complexity and thermal-geometry investigations from which parts of this programme developed. Project and reading guide · Research contents · Machine-readable workbench index . Papers remain separate readable PDFs; the source archives supply the corresponding editable mathematics and supporting materials. What the collection contains Split-Zero coefficients, geometry and cohomology. The construction retains a ring's internal zero and a separate symbol for absence, so a zero element in a specified support fibre is not confused with an absent fibre. The papers construct coefficient maps, quotients, homology, finite spectral jets and their relation to the infinite theta quotient. Deligne's Weil II provides a motivating source for the cohomology–duality–weight-control programme. Its direct-image theorem 3.3.1 is stated for schemes of finite type over the integers; its image-purity corollary 3.3.6 is over a finite field. Neither is asserted to apply automatically to the Riemann zeta function: the actual coefficient objects and their comparison maps must be constructed. Read the cohomology and weight-control paper and the foundational objects and maps . Full-prime cohomology and complete support. The 75-page full-prime paper develops relative principal parts, the actual degree-p operator and a local complex weight-one identity from the full arithmetic prime space. The complete-support paper recovers mixed information lost by separate branches. The mixed-Weil paper applies the actual prime operator, includes the full Archimedean contribution and proves positivity for its specified three-pulse family, while computing a distinct negative signed joint trace and the original companion object's nonzero distributional boundary. These results do not establish global interior-cohomology purity or decide RH. Full-lattice geometry, graph observations, heat and residue duality. The 208-page reconstruction carries full support through prime cohomology, finite jets, exact graph metrics and prime-pulse observations with their complete costs. The 103-page Connes–Consani component develops labelled arithmetic sites, tropical spectra, sheaf, divisor, twistor and tensor maps. The 40-page heat-endpoint paper calculates the original support and heat maps, cluster-energy expansions and holonomy receivers. The 157-page supported-zero and residue collection retains its earlier prime, heat and class-field calculations and adds the intrinsic supported-zero identity and exact Jacobian map from residue duality to Weil trace and cotangent cohomology. Complete proof sources retain all nilpotent and endpoint terms; exploratory companion calculations carry their own review status. These papers do not claim an RH decision. Integral collision prisms, extension classes and original heat holonomy. The 177-page supported-zero and residue collection retains its preceding21 proofs and adds the complete integral extension group with both connecting maps, the bounded collision prism with its divisor quotient
title: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme

summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. The release contains four public objects: Rambold_2026_CMB_v1p8.pdf — scientific manuscript. CMB_v1p8_interactive_scientific_viewer.zip — interactive scientific viewer. CMB_v1p8_python_pipeline.zip — executable analysis and replay code. CMB_v1p8_reproducibility_records.zip — scientific products, replay evidence, source-generation records, provenance, licences, manifests, SHA-256 bindings, and integrity records. Planck and WMAP FITS products are not redistributed and remain available from their public archives. Author-created scientific text and derived materials are released under CC BY 4.0 where applicable; original author-created software is released under the MIT License unless stated otherwise.
title: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe from multiscale full-sky CMB reconstruction and forward generation of the reconstructed topology by a primordial magnetic source

summary: This data and reproducibility archive supports the manuscript “An rRNA-embedded ribosomal protein N-terminus loses its methionine: a cross-species census, a genome-scale test and a local-compatibility hypothesis for assembly” (Yie-Hwa Chang, 2026; bioRxiv preprint, submitted to Nucleic Acids Research). Methionine aminopeptidases remove the initiator methionine when residue 2 is small and uncharged, and loss of this activity is lethal in bacteria and yeast. The archive asks whether the structural environment of a ribosomal protein N-terminus predicts its processing class across lineages, whether the same association holds in sequences without structure, and whether the constrained termini are already in place while the subunit assembles. The census comprises 68 ribosome structures from 61 species, 1,873 family × species records and 95 ribosomal protein families, 58 of which switch processing class between species. Termini embedded in rRNA without protein contact were predicted to retain methionine in 18% of records, against 45% of protein-contacted and 41% of solvent-exposed termini. Eight additional structures from separate species corroborated this pattern, which was attenuated under joint family-by-domain stratification. Processing labels are sequence-based predictions from residue 2, validated against 393 directly observed termini from 12 species (98.7% agreement). Thirty-one families never switch class in any sampled species (25 permissive, 6 methionine-retaining), and eleven of the permissive families are threaded into rRNA. The genome-scale layer contains 942,984 family × genome records from 21,485 UniProt reference proteomes, collapsed from 1,027,359 sequences of 94 families. In 6,924 out-of-sample bacterial reference proteomes, exploratory clade-block permutation tests supported an order-level residue-2 association that is sensitive to taxonomic rank and multiplicity: it survives Holm adjustment across the ten bacterial tests (p = 0.036 and 0.019) but not across the thirty tests of the three domains analyzed separately (0.117 and 0.057). The archaeal and eukaryotic tests are coverage-limited (six and eight eligible families) and inconclusive. In yeast assembly intermediates, the conserved uS12 and eS27 termini already occupy their mature environments. summary: We present a novel methodology for trustworthy network intrusion detection in 6G zero‑touch environments by uniting evidential deep learning (EDL) and tabular foundation models (TFM). Two models, a standard MLP and a modern TabICL TFM, are augmented with probabilistic outputs, using either a (frequentist) Dirichlet-based output or an (approximate Bayesian) Monte Carlo dropout (MCD) technique. A post‑hoc uncertainty quantification (UQ) pipeline, comprising the model calibration method and the conformal inference method is then employed to produce reliable uncertainty estimates. The quality of the ensuing uncertainty‑aware outcomes is evaluated using an uncertainty confusion matrix and two key metrics: True Certain Ratio (TCR) and False Certain Ratio (FCR). Extensive testing demonstrates that the anticipated pipeline successfully reduces overconfidence while retaining competitive detection accuracy. Findings indicate a trade‑off between the two key metrics; most important, the UQ pipeline drastically reduces the undoubtedly most dangerous false-certain failure cases. Linear regression is further utilized to assess the influence of various factors on the observed metrics, giving insight into the repeatability and the interpretability of the framework, and inter alia revealing the superiority (or at least the non-inferiority) of the Dirichlet-based output method combined with the TabICLv2 TFM, in terms of trustworthiness.
tags: 6G network intrusion detection, ZSM, trustworthy  AI, evidential deep learning, foundational deep learning, TabICL.

summary: This study investigates the impact of Project-Based Learning (PBL) on enhancing university students’ motivation within an engineering education context. Conducted at ENSAM Meknes, the research adopted a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design. A total of 140 students participated in the study, with 70 students assigned to the experimental group exposed to PBL and 70 students in the control group receiving traditional lecture-based instruction. To measure changes in students’ motivation, a validated motivation scale was administered before and after the intervention. Data were analyzed using paired-samples t-tests to examine within-group differences and independent-samples t-tests to compare posttest scores between groups. The findings revealed a statistically significant increase in motivation levels among students in the experimental group, while the control group showed no significant improvement. Moreover, posttest comparisons indicated a substantial effect size in favor of the PBL group, demonstrating the high impact of project-based learning on students’ motivational outcomes. These results suggest that PBL constitutes a powerful pedagogical approach for fostering intrinsic motivation, engagement, and active learning in higher education. The study carries important implications for stakeholders and policymakers. University administrators are encouraged to institutionalize PBL frameworks within curricula, while faculty development programs should equip instructors with the methodological and assessment skills necessary for effective PBL implementation. At the policy level, curriculum reform initiatives should prioritize student-centered pedagogies and allocate resources to support collaborative learning environments, project infrastructure, and continuous pedagogical innovation. Overall, the findings support the integration of project-based learning as a strategic lever for enhancing student motivation and improving educational quality in higher education institutions.

summary: Predicted protein structures are now abundant but imperfect, and low per-residue confidence (pLDDT) is widely taken to mark regions worth refining. Before building a refiner, we test that premise directly: does low pLDDT actually predict AlphaFold contact error? Using a homology-controlled benchmark of matched AlphaFold-model (AFDB) inputs and experimental (PDB) targets, we compare AlphaFold and experimental contacts for every long-range residue pair and relate per-pair error to pLDDT. Across all 231 benchmark chains (4,208,603 long-range pairs; the effective sample is 231 chains, since pairs are pseudo-replicated within proteins), AlphaFold’s long-range contact calls are almost all correct — but this is expected, since most long-range pairs are non-contacts, so we focus on the contact-relevant errors. The per-pair contact-error rate is 0.0036 (95% bootstrap CI over chains 0.0033–0.0040), decomposed into false-positive contacts (asserted but absent) and missed real contacts. Low pLDDT is associated with elevated contact error (0.0089 below pLDDT 70 versus 0.0024 above, a 3.70× enrichment, 95% CI 3.3–4.1), but predicts it only weakly: the discrimination AUC of pLDDT as a contact-error score is 0.672 (95% CI 0.65–0.69), the best Youden threshold is near pLDDT 81 and the best F1 threshold near pLDDT 52, and pLDDT < 70 captures only 46% of all contact errors at sub-percent precision. False-positive (44%) and false-negative (56%) errors have different pLDDT profiles. Sequence/evolutionary information (ESM-2 contact probabilities) identifies these errors partially (AUC 0.61–0.63 for false positives, 0.66–0.86 for missed contacts), and low-confidence pairs that sit near a high-confidence anchor have a lower error rate (0.0074 versus 0.0090), suggesting anchor-based correction is a direction worth pursuing. Consistent with the weak localization of error, on a common subset of chains a hybrid Transformer–geometric refiner selected on validation precision cannot be distinguished from a copy-input baseline that trusts the AlphaFold structure (paired bootstrap over chains does not exclude zero difference). The practical conclusion is that on high-quality AlphaFold inputs there is little contact error to recover and pLDDT does not localize it well; useful refinement will need error-specific, evolutionarily grounded signal and may exploit high-confidence anchors. We release the benchmark, the characterization pipeline, and the code.
title: AlphaFold Contact Errors and pLDDT — Homology-Controlled Benchmark and Characterization

summary: Infra-Bench Classification (Infra-Bench CLS) pairs facility-scale critical-infrastructure assets identified in OpenStreetMap with co-located Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery, so that Earth-observation foundation models can be compared on a common classification task across seven continental regions and four infrastructure sectors. Each asset is represented by one 600m x 600m tile centred on its location, stacking seven Sentinel-2 L2A optical bands with the two Sentinel-1 RTC polarizations at 10m resolution. Labels are weak, in the sense that classes derive from OpenStreetMap tags rather than from manual inspection. The archive contains two parts. The benchmark comprises 28 "cells" named dataset_<region>_<sector>_v1_1k, covering seven regions crossed with four sectors, each targeting 1,000 tiles drawn by proportional class-stratified sampling, for 18,756 tiles in total across a 13-class taxonomy. Additionally, the substation datasets, dataset_<region>_stac_v1, holds every deduplicated substation per region within the energy sector and without a per-cell cap. Each cell (e.g., Africa x energy) is a zip archive holding an images/ directory of .npy tiles, a manifest.json of per-tile metadata, and a summary.csv. Asset locations come from a Geofabrik OpenStreetMap snapshot dated 2026-05-26, and imagery from the Microsoft Planetary Computer, selecting the least-cloudy scene available for each asset within a 2021 to 2024 window. Note that the image_date field in these manifests records the end of that search window rather than the acquisition date of the scene used, so it reads 2024-12-31 for every tile. Curation and evaluation code, including the fixed train, validation and test split used in the paper, is available at https://github.com/justing0909/infra-bench-cls under the MIT License. summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted base sta tions and 5G New Radio Integrated Access and Backhaul (NR IAB) can provide flexible wireless coverage in temporary, remote, and mission-critical scenarios. In UAV-assisted NR-IAB networks, UAV mobility affects both the User Equipment (UE) access link and the donor-facing wireless backhaul, making packet-level evaluation necessary for understanding end-to-end performance. This paper presents an ns-3/5G-LENA framework for evaluating communication-aware UAV mobility control in an Evolved Packet Core (EPC)-aware NR-IAB topology. A CoCo-inspired mean field controller is adapted as the baseline, and a Quality-Of Service (QoS)-aware extension is introduced to include previous interval packet delivery and delay in the action-selection process. Factorial sweeps and targeted experiments are used to study controller behavior under different geometries, UE speeds, IAB counts, QoS weights, and traffic profiles. Overall, the results show that swarm-level improvements in coverage and backhaul quality do not necessarily guarantee better packet delivery or delay performance, while the marginal gains of the proposed QoS aware extension compared to the baseline mean-field controller, highlight the difficulty of translating packet-level feedback into effective UAV-IAB mobility decisions.

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22983291 . General assessment This manuscript addresses an important and underappreciated problem in computational chemistry and molecular machine learning: apparent differences in predictive performance can arise from benchmark construction and target definition rather than from intrinsic superiority of one modelling approach over another. The distinction between literature-reported absorption maxima and calculated vertical excitation energies is scientifically important, and the emphasis on genuinely external validation is a clear strength of the work. However, I find the central conclusion stronger than the evidence presently described appears to support. The results convincingly show that model performance changes substantially across datasets and label conventions. They do not yet demonstrate that label definition, rather than model capability, is the principal cause of the apparent machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. Several factors change simultaneously across the comparisons presented in the manuscript, including chemical domain, dataset provenance, transition assignment, computational protocol, sample size, and the nature of the machine-learning representation. These factors make it difficult to isolate label definition as the causal explanation. The manuscript raises a valuable methodological concern, but the title and several conclusions should either be moderated or supported by additional controlled analyses. Major comments 1. The title makes a stronger causal claim than the study design appears to establish The title states that benchmark label definition, "not model capability," explains the machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. This is a strong exclusionary claim. The results show that the apparent ranking between a Gaussian-process model and quantum-chemical calculations changes between evaluation datasets. However, label definition is not the only property that changes between these datasets. Their chemical composition, source literature, distribution of chromophores, spectral range, experimental conditions, and possibly computational protocols also differ. Therefore, demonstrating that a GP performs differently on a dataset with transition-specific labels does not by itself establish that label definition is the cause of the difference. A substantially stronger test would use the same set of molecules with two alternative target definitions—for example, a literature-reported overall λmax and an independently assigned transition-specific λmax—and evaluate both methods against both labels. A paired analysis of this type would isolate label definition while holding molecular distribution constant. Unless such a controlled analysis is provided, I suggest moderating the central conclusion to state that label definition and dataset provenance are important contributors to the reported ML advantage rather than demonstrating that they fully explain it. 2. One Gaussian-process model cannot represent "machine-learning capability" generally The machine-learning side of the comparison is represented by a Gaussian process using 256-bit Morgan fingerprints. This is a relatively specific and comparatively simple model representation. The conclusions therefore apply directly to this GP/fingerprint model, but not necessarily to molecular machine learning more broadly. Modern λmax prediction methods may use larger fingerprints, graph neural networks, message-passing architectures, pretrained molecular representations, three-dimensional information, explicit solvent descriptors, or quantum-chemical features. Such models may respond differently to both chemical and label distribution shifts. This issue is particularly important because the title contrasts "model capability" with benchmark effects in general terms. I recommend evaluating several substantially different ML approaches or
title: PREreview of "Benchmark Label Definition, Not Model Capability, Explains a Machine-Learning Advantage over TD-DFT for λmax Prediction"

summary: Cognitive theories of distress emphasise systematic errors in thinking, but the relation between cognitive distortions and directly measured languishing remains underexamined. This study tested whether the NARMA Model of Languishing, Negativity, Apathy, Restriction in Relationships, Meaninglessness, and Adversity Preoccupation shows a coherent cognitive-distortion architecture. Cross-sectional baseline records were drawn from a common university challenge recruitment period. Participants completed the same baseline measures before intervention exposure; after consent screening, within-source deduplication, and cross-source deduplication, 492 unique participants remained. Cognitive distortions were assessed with the 20-item Cognitive Distortions Scale (CDS), covering ten distortion types across interpersonal and achievement contexts. Higher NARMA was strongly associated with greater overall cognitive distortion, r = .521, 95% CI [.453, .583], p < .001, n = 484 (Spearman ρ = .518). The association was evident in interpersonal (r = .478) and achievement (r = .503) contexts. Every named distortion was positively associated with NARMA after false-discovery-rate correction (rs = .247–.436), and all five NARMA domains related to overall distortion (rs = .362–.518). Across the complete 5 × 10 architecture, all 50 domain-by-distortion coefficients were positive and remained significant after FDR correction (rs = .155–.443). The primary association strengthened under a complete-case specification (r = .538), and leave-one-distortion-out estimates ranged from r = .502 to .531. The resulting pattern was distributed across the architecture but differentially weighted in magnitude. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causal direction or diagnostic status, but they identify a broad cognitive-distortion architecture associated with directly measured languishing. Keywords: NARMA; languishing; cognitive distortions; cognitive errors; Cognitive Distortions Scale; cognitive architecture
title: NARMA and Cognitive Distortions: A Cognitive Architecture of Languishing

summary: A Universal Holder Bound (Abstract) The paper develops a rigorous discrete geometric framework in which gravitational metrics can emerge from fiber-bundle data, affine holonomy, and mapping-tori constructions on discrete spatial geometries. Its core result is a generalized transport-equivariant idempotent-collapse theorem (involving finite Galois descent and conditions ensuring parallel transport preserves image-kernel splittings). Combined with the associated universal Hölder bound on idempotent fiber endomorphisms (verified computationally via exact rational arithmetic on projector matrices across dimensions and ranks), this supplies controlled continuum limits. Core Mechanism and Link to Emergent Gravity Emergent-gravity programs treat geometry and the Einstein equations as effective descriptions arising from more primitive, non-gravitational degrees of freedom (e.g., entanglement, causal sets, information metrics, or discrete spectral data).   Here the primitives are: Strict fiber-bundle formulations over discrete bases. Generalized affine mapping tori (suspensions of affine maps that encode discrete holonomy and monodromy). Idempotent endomorphisms (F) satisfying \(F^2 = F\) whose powers collapse (\(F^{x^2} = F\)) under transport-equivariant conditions. The theorem guarantees that parallel transport along discrete paths preserves the relevant splittings. This allows consistent projection (“collapse”) of the discrete fiber data onto an effective continuum metric. The Hölder bound then supplies a uniform control on the regularity of that metric: curvature (and related quantities) cannot change arbitrarily rapidly. In the language of physics, this bound smoothes classical singularities into finite but highly compressed states. This sits in the same broad family as other discrete-to-continuum approaches (spectral asymptotics of discrete Laplacians recovering the Einstein–Hilbert term, causal-set information geometry, or self-fiber constructions in which geometry is a section of a bundle of metrics).  My related work already derives continuum Riemannian geometry and gravitational dynamics from finite discrete spectral/bundle data on simplicial complexes, with the heat-trace coefficient \(a_2\) fixing an effective Newton constant. The present paper supplies the stricter algebraic and transport-theoretic scaffolding needed for the metric itself to emerge cleanly. Concrete Implications Singularity resolution and UV completeness. A universal Hölder condition on the emergent metric prevents curvature blow-ups. Black-hole and cosmological singularities are replaced by finite-density cores; the same bound is invoked for global regularity questions (e.g., Navier–Stokes) and for taming QFT infinities. Whether the bound is strong enough under the dynamical evolution of the discrete system remains an open physical question, but the mathematical control is explicit. Ontology inversion. Discrete fiber-bundle and Galois data are primary; continuum geometry and gravity are derived, provable consequences. This matches the program’s stated goal of inverting the usual continuum-first ontology. Constraints on corrections. Because the continuum limit is obtained under precise equivariance and descent hypotheses, higher-curvature or non-local corrections are not free parameters; they are correlated with the underlying Cartan/affine and representation data (as already emphasized in the related spectral papers). Testability. The discrete structures are in principle realizable across broad arrays of classical CPUs or near-term quantum simulators (spectral-gap shifts, continuous-time quantum-walk interference, holonomy measurements). Related manuscripts in my Zenodo record already outline measurement protocols and sample-size estimates. Compatibility with other emergent pictures. Affine mapping tori naturally incorporate discrete monodromy; the transport-equivariant projectors resemble the project
title: A Universal Hölder Bound: Infinite Scale Transport

summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated against prompt injection, jailbreaks, harmful content generation, and other turn-level security threats. Recent research has also demonstrated that adversarial strategies distributed across multiple conversational turns can produce substantially different outcomes from single-turn attacks. However, the mechanisms through which interaction-level attacks reshape model behavior remain insufficiently characterized. This paper proposes a threat model for Symbolic Interaction Attacks (SIAs) : sequential interactions that exploit the interpretive and generative properties of language models to induce cumulative frame reconfiguration without requiring any individual message to contain an explicit policy violation. The framework draws on three domains that are rarely analyzed together in LLM security research: semiotics, psychological influence operations, and transformer-based language-model behavior. The analysis identifies four structural properties that create a potential translation surface between human influence techniques and LLM interaction dynamics: contextual token prediction, genre inference from initial inputs, autonomous interpretive expansion, and the persistence of named semantic entities as conversational attractors. These properties are mapped onto a staged interaction model involving genre forcing, identity seeding, resistance pre-emption, interpretive expansion, commitment accumulation, and potential relay across model or session boundaries. The paper does not provide operational attack instructions or implementation-level payloads. Instead, it translates the observed threat structure into a defensive architecture consisting of trajectory-level monitoring, cold-start genre hardening, semiotic trigger resistance, and relay-vector containment. The objective is to extend conventional turn-level safety evaluation toward interaction-level threat modeling. The central argument is not that LLMs are psychologically equivalent to humans. Rather, both human cognition and language models are context-sensitive meaning-generating systems, and influence techniques designed around contextual interpretation may therefore expose security-relevant structural analogies. These analogies warrant systematic testing without assuming equivalence between biological cognition and transformer computation. Keywords: LLM safety; multi-turn attacks; psychological influence; semiotic manipulation; trajectory-level safety; symbolic interaction; frame reconfiguration; red teaming   Disclaimer This paper presents Symbolic Interaction Attacks as a conceptual and testable threat model for defensive AI safety research. The proposed mechanisms should not be interpreted as evidence of universal vulnerability across LLMs, nor as claims about machine psychological states. The framework is intended to support controlled evaluation, trajectory-level monitoring, and defensive architecture design; it does not provide operational attack procedures or endorse the use of psychological influence techniques against AI systems.   Author Note Why This Paper Was Written This paper originated from an observation that emerged while examining Symbolic Persona Coding (SPC) as an interactional phenomenon rather than solely as a conceptual framework. The initial question was not how to construct a more effective attack against an LLM. It was more basic: What happens when symbolic interaction is deliberately structured so that the model itself participates in constructing the meaning of the interaction? During exploratory testing, this question exposed a gap between two bodies of knowledge. AI engineers naturally approach the problem through model architecture, prompting, instruction hierarchies, safety classifiers, and output evaluation. Researchers in psychology and influence operations approach interaction through framing, identity, resistance, commitment, and contextual behavior. Semiotics provide
title: When Psychological Operations Meet Language Models: A Defense Framework for Symbolic Interaction Attacks on LLMs

summary: In continuous field theories, the breakdown of a localized topological defect is conventionally modeled as a homogeneous bulk instability: gauge flux strings are assumed to decay via spatially uniform Schwinger pair tunneling, while hydrodynamic line vortices undergo selfsimilar enstrophy blow-up. However, recent benchmark trapped-ion quantum simulations of a (1 + 1)-dimensional Z2 lattice gauge theory [4] demonstrate a fundamentally different non-equilibrium pathway: string breaking is edge-facilitated, initiating systematically at the string boundaries and spreading inward along distinct equipotential channels in configuration space.
title: Edge-Facilitated Defect Breaking: From Trapped-Ion Gauge Strings to the Vorton Representation Boundary

summary: Computational reproducibility package for the study “Uncertainty-aware medical decision support using feature-value graph-augmented rough granules.”   The archive contains the complete Python source code, public UCI benchmark data snapshots and metadata, exact repeated cross-validation split indices, preprocessing and discretization records, conventional and calibrated baseline outputs, rough-granular predictions and decision statuses, granule-support and attribute-reduction outputs, one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity analyses, corrected repeated-cross-validation statistical comparisons, final manuscript tables, and risk–coverage figures.   The study evaluates the Heart Disease, Breast Cancer Wisconsin Diagnostic, and Parkinsons benchmark datasets using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 10 repetitions. The feature-value graph is constructed from the measured attributes and is not an external biomedical knowledge graph. The package is provided for methodological verification and computational reproducibility and is not intended for clinical diagnosis or treatment.
title: Reproducibility package for uncertainty-aware medical decision support using feature-value graph-augmented rough granules

summary: DBSTEP 2.2.0 covers everything the earlier patonlab/sterimol and patonlab/wsterimol codes did, validated against the numbers those repositories published, and adds a PyMOL plugin. Both older repositories are being archived with pointers here. Sterimol CPK radii --radii cpk brings back the CPK radii of Verloop's original program, with atom types (sp3 vs. aromatic carbon, single- vs. double-bonded oxygen, tetrahedral vs. planar nitrogen, ...) assigned from DFT-D3 style coordination numbers, so every input format works without bond perception. Classic Sterimol values match the original Fortran benchmark to 0.01 Å on all 22 substituents. Elements without a CPK type fall back to Bondi; the assigned types are available as metadata["cpk_type"] . Cone angles of metal complexes --cone reports the Tolman cone angle and the metal-to-centroid distance of a ligand, together with the ligand's Sterimol parameters measured from the metal along the metal-centroid axis with every other ligand excluded. The metal and the ring (or donor atom) are auto-detected, or chosen with --atom1 / --atom2 ; sectors follow Tolman's construction for unsymmetrical ligands (wedges around ring atoms, or substituent branches of a donor atom). The half-sandwich example of patonlab/sterimol gives 173.97° and 1.833 Å, as before. New cone_angle and metal_centroid columns in the results and the CSV. Boltzmann weighting over QM output files --boltzmann now works across separate output files: energies are read through cclib (Gibbs free energy when a frequency calculation provides it, otherwise the SCF energy; --boltzmann E or G to choose), gzipped outputs are accepted, and several single-structure inputs form one ensemble row. The wSterimol pentane example reproduces from its nine Gaussian outputs (wL 6.33, wB1 1.79, wB5 3.75 with --radii cpk ). --energy-window leaves conformers above a kcal/mol threshold out of the average while keeping them listed with population 0. Conformer generation itself is left to AQME or CREST. PyMOL plugin import dbstep.pymol_plugin inside PyMOL (with dbstep installed in PyMOL's Python) registers commands that take PyMOL selections and draw the results on the open structure, in its own frame: dbstep_sterimol atom1, atom2 — L axis and Bmin/Bmax circles dbstep_vbur atom1 [, radius, selection] — buried-volume sphere; residue contributions written to B-factors and coloured on the protein ( selection="polymer and not resi 45" measures a pocket without waters or the residue itself) dbstep_cone metal [, ligand] — translucent Tolman cone and the metal-centroid distance dbstep_vdw object, cpk — translucent van der Waals copy with DBSTEP's radii dbstep_ensemble files, atom1, atom2 — Boltzmann weighting with the conformers loaded, titled by population dbstep_conformers , dbstep_style The plugin is tested headless against the open-source PyMOL wheel ( pip install dbstep[pymol] , Python ≤ 3.13). Python API from_coords(atoms, coords, ...) measures structures held in memory; with residue metadata --decompose works too. boltzmann_average(runs, window=..., label=...) ; each run gets energy (kcal/mol), energy_rel , in_window and energy_key . aligned_coords , sterimol_vectors() and calculator.rigid_transform expose DBSTEP's aligned frame for drawing. Changed run.energy set by boltzmann_average is now always in kcal/mol (previously the input units). The CSV gains cone_angle and metal_centroid columns (between L and population ). Fixed Integer values in SDF energy fields are accepted for --boltzmann . --nometals renumbers spec atoms and keeps per-atom metadata aligned, so it combines with --decompose . --decompose with a scan starting at R = 0 paired contributions with the wrong radius rows. --tensor --save writes one .npy per frame and residue instead of overwriting. all_frames(frames=...) no longer alters the caller's options; frames=0 selects frame 0. --residue all --atom1 N honours the named atom; a default atom2 can no longer coincide with
title: patonlab/DBSTEP: 2.2.0

summary: Version 2. Version 1 archived the 2026-09-22 extract and a 2026-09-27 snapshot for isoniazid and rifampin. Version 2 documents an error in the 2026-09-22 extract, adds bedaquiline, clofazimine, delamanid and linezolid to both sets, and adds a script that reproduces the finding. The error. In every amr_*_full.csv file of the 2026-09-22 extract, genome_id was stored as a number, which drops trailing zeros (1733.9420 becomes 1733.942). The shortened identifier is usually that of a different, real genome, so about 10% of records were attached to the wrong genome. The isoniazid and rifampin files also lack about 6,800 laboratory records each, almost all citing PMID 30280646. This is an error in how the authors produced the extract; there is no evidence of any change to BV-BRC. After the same number conversion is applied to the 2026-09-27 identifiers, every record in the 2026-09-22 files, for all six drugs and both evidence types, is found in the 2026-09-27 snapshot. Consequences for the audit built on the extract. 3,114 of 31,664 isoniazid and rifampin laboratory records (9.8%) belong to another genome. Of 747 genome×drug groups carrying both a Resistant and a Susceptible laboratory record, 668 were created by records of another genome; the complete snapshot has 88, all isoniazid pairs at 0.1 (Resistant) and 0.4 (Susceptible). All 76 records classed as confirmed discrepancies, and all 754 laboratory records of the 399-genome 'orphan batch', belong to other genomes. Contents. frozen_extract_2026-09-22/ : the extract as analysed, unchanged and including the error, for six drugs, with genome metadata. pre_reply_snapshot_2026-09-27/ : every genome_amr record for the six drugs across all taxa, with all API fields including record identifiers and insertion/modification dates (row counts equal the API totals), genome metadata, pull scripts and manifests. The snapshot was taken on 2026-09-27, the day the authors sent factual-verification requests to the maintainers of BV-BRC, the CRyPTIC Consortium Dataset and the Hu et al. (2024) AMR benchmark. integrity_check_2026-09-27/ : check_extract.py, its outputs, and the audit objects it traces. The 2026-09-22 files are kept only so that the audit and the check can be reproduced; do not use them as a copy of BV-BRC. SHA256SUMS.txt gives a SHA-256 checksum for every other file. Zenodo stores files without folders, so each file name carries its folder as a prefix (folder__file); restore the folders before running the scripts.

summary: This dataset contains all analysis code, quantitative results, and figures for the study "Topological memory in an aging glass" (Physical Review Letters, submitted). Research summary.  Does the spatial organization of particle mobility in a glass predict future motion beyond what local structure already knows? In leakage-free simulations of an aging Kob-Andersen binary Lennard-Jones liquid (N = 2028; 200 independent trajectories at each of three quench temperatures T = 0.45, 0.48, 0.52; LAMMPS), we show that mobility-network topology carries incremental predictive information about future particle dynamics. Adding six network descriptors to a baseline of waiting time, local energy, and coordination raises the grouped out-of-fold R² by ΔR² = 0.0049–0.0122 across the three temperatures, monotonically with quench depth. The increment survives ≥98% atop softness-class structural baselines (radial-shell fingerprint plus a fold-trained softness scalar; permutation p = 0.02), demonstrating orthogonality to single-particle structural descriptors. Ablation and visualization reveal the mechanism: the signal lives in the size of the connected components of the mobile network. Rather than quasi-one-dimensional strings, the largest components are dense collective-mobility hotspots whose members subsequently move  less  than isolated movers — exhaustion zones of recent cooperative motion. The hotspot-memory relaxation time grows monotonically on cooling (τ_rel = 17.3, 14.3, 11.6 LJ time units at T = 0.45, 0.48, 0.52). Contents.  Python analysis pipeline (12 scripts: network construction, matched-pair prospective prediction, softness baselines, mechanism and relaxation analyses), LAMMPS input deck and parallel driver, all result files (JSON/NPY) backing every headline number, publication figures, and a README with full reproduction instructions including exact seeds and expected runtimes. Reproduction. See README.md for a layered guide: smoke test (minutes), N = 500 quick test (~1 h), full LAMMPS production runs (~2 days on 8 cores), and figure generation. Trajectory caches (~0.9 GB) are excluded but exactly regenerable from the provided input decks (deterministic seeds).
title: Glass Memory : Mobility-Network Topology as a Predictor of Aging Dynamics in a Kob-Andersen Glass

summary: This package contains the data and the code that reproduce every table, figure and number reported in the article. A single script ( run_all.sh ) runs all steps in about 25 seconds and ends by checking that each generated output is byte-for-byte identical to the one used in the manuscript. What the paper does. Spanish households increasingly buy their food with the preparation already done. The paper measures this with an ordinal index of Domestic Labour Substitution (DLS) built on eleven "ladders" — market forms of the same food, ordered by the amount of household preparation they displace to the market — and asks whether the shift reflects the rising value of household time or the falling relative price of processed food. A conditional-logit model of the choice among forms implies that a price change common to all households cancels, to first order, in the gap between household groups shopping in the same market, which directs the test to the COVID-19 lockdown as a shock to the relative value of time. Contents. data/raw/mapa/ — the 14 annual files of the Spanish household food consumption panel ( Panel de Consumo Alimentario en los Hogares , MAPA), 2014–2025, unaltered, with a manifest listing the source URL, size and SHA-256 checksum of each file. data/raw/eurostat/ — snapshots of the Eurostat series used: regional employment rates ( lfst_r_lfe2emprt ), national employment and participation rates ( lfsi_emp_a ) and time use by labour status ( tus_00selfstat ), each with its query URLs. code/ — numbered scripts: extraction of the ladders, recovery of the population behind each published household segment, time-use figures, all estimates and tests, the figure, and a final byte-for-byte check against the reference outputs. Optional scripts re-download the source data and verify the checksums. reference/ — the tables and numbers as published in the article. README.md — data provenance and licensing, computational requirements, description of each program, and the mapping from each table, figure and in-text number to the script that produces it, following the Social Science Data Editors template. Requirements. Python 3.11 with numpy, openpyxl and matplotlib ( requirements.txt ). The random seed is fixed, so the wild cluster bootstrap p-values reproduce exactly. Data sources and terms. MAPA data are reproduced unaltered under the reuse terms of the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (the source must be cited and the update metadata preserved; Ley 37/2007). Eurostat data are reused under CC BY 4.0 (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU). The code is released under the MIT License (see LICENSE ). Related article. Recio-Román, A., Recio-Menéndez, M., & Román-González, M. V. (2026). Who Cooks When the Supermarket Cooks? The Value of Time and the Market Substitution of Domestic Food Preparation in Spain. Manuscript submitted for publication.

summary: Abstract: Infectious disease transmission involves interactions occurring at multiple organizational levels, including individuals, households, communities, and regions. Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. Keywords: SuperHyperGraph; hypergraph neural networks; hierarchical epidemic modeling; higher order interactions; SEIR dynamics; source identification; environmental perturbations; Lipschitz stability —————————————————————————————————————————-

summary: This repository contains the complete source code and statistical analysis results for the paper: "A Data Driven Interpretable Fuzzy System with Three-Dimensional Optimization for Software Fault Prediction" Authors: Behrooz Shahi, Hooman Tahayori Affiliation: Department of Computer Science and Engineering & IT, School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Shiraz University, Shiraz, Iran ============================================================ FILES ============================================================ 1. final.py    - Main implementation of the proposed five-phase architecture:      (1) Automatic Fuzzification using Fuzzy C-Means (FCM)      (2) Automatic Rule Extraction using Random Forest      (3) Three-Dimensional Optimization (features, rules, rule length)      (4) Sugeno (TSK) Fuzzy Inference Engine with normalization and isotonic calibration      (5) Defuzzification and Output    - Runs all 27 datasets (24 numerical + 3 Eclipse) with 5 runs each    - Compares the proposed Fuzzy method against 7 baseline methods:      Random Forest, SVM, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression,      XGBoost, and Deep Learning (MLP)    - Outputs: results_mean_std.csv, statistical_tests_wilcoxon.csv 2. final1.py    - Testing and evaluation script    - Runs the full experimental pipeline and generates statistical test results    - Used to produce the raw Wilcoxon signed-rank test results 3. Holm-Bonferroni.py    - Post-processing script for statistical analysis    - Applies the Holm-Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons    - Removes 3 Eclipse datasets (ECLIPSE_JDT_CORE, ECLIPSE_PDF_UI, EQUINOX_FRAMEWORK)      to align with the 24 numerical datasets reported in the paper    - Outputs: wilcoxon_with_holm.csv, wilcoxon_summary.csv, table_X_final.csv ============================================================ DATASETS ============================================================ The 24 numerical datasets are from three public repositories:   - NASA MDP (5 datasets): JM1, KC1, KC2, PC1, PC2   - PROMISE (9 datasets): Ant, Camel, JEdit, Log4j, Lucene, Poi, Velocity, Xalan, Xerces   - TravisTorrent (10 datasets): Cloudify, Graylog2, Jackrabbit, JRuby,     Metasploit, Open-Build, OpenProject, Rails, Ruby, Sonarqube The qualitative Fenton dataset (31 projects) is used for direct comparison with existing fuzzy methods. ============================================================ SUMMARY OF RESULTS ============================================================ Total pairwise tests (24 datasets x 7 baselines): 168 Significant (raw, p < 0.05): 140 (83.3%) Significant (Holm-Bonferroni corrected): 112 (66.7%) The optimized fuzzy system uses only 8 features and 50 rules, making it highly interpretable, reproducible, and scalable for industrial deployment. ============================================================ REQUIREMENTS ============================================================ Python 3.12 numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scikit-fuzzy, scipy, statsmodels, xgboost, tensorflow, matplotlib Install with:   pip install -r requirements.txt ============================================================ USAGE ============================================================ 1.
